title.zh: 卷49 列傳第14 牛弘
title.raw: 卷49 列傳第14 牛弘 Volume 49 Biographies 14: Niu Hong

sentences.zh: 隋書卷四十九列傳第十四

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume Forty-Nine, Biographies Fourteen
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, 49th year of Volume, fourteenth year of Biographies

sentences.zh: ○牛弘

translations.literal: ○ Niu Hong
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong

sentences.zh: 牛弘，字裡仁，安定鶉觚人也，本姓裛氏。

translations.literal: Niu Hong, courtesy name Liren, was a native of Chingui in Anding; his original surname was the Yi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong, courtesy name Liren, was a native of Chingui in Anding. His family originally bore the surname Yi.

sentences.zh: 祖熾，郡中正。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chi was a district impartial judge.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chi served as a district impartial judge.

sentences.zh: 父允，魏侍中、工部尚書、臨涇公，賜姓為牛氏。

translations.literal: His father Yun was Wei Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, and Duke of Linjing; he was granted the surname Niu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yun served the Wei as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, and Duke of Linjing, and was granted the surname Niu.

sentences.zh: 弘初在繈褓，有相者見之，謂其父曰：「此兒當貴，善愛養之。」

translations.literal: When Hong was still in swaddling clothes, a physiognomist saw him and said to his father: "This boy is destined for eminence; cherish and nurture him well.
translations.idiomatic: While Hong was still an infant, a physiognomist who saw him told his father, "This boy is destined for greatness. Raise him with care.

sentences.zh: 及長，須貌甚偉，性寬裕，好學博聞。

translations.literal: When he grew up, his beard and appearance were very imposing; his nature was generous and broad-minded, and he loved learning and was widely informed.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he had a full beard and an imposing appearance. He was generous by nature, loved learning, and was widely read.

sentences.zh: 在周，起家中外府記室、內史上士。

translations.literal: Under the Zhou, he began his career as recorder for the inner and outer prefectures and as Senior Clerk in the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Zhou, he entered service as recorder for the inner and outer prefectures and as Senior Clerk in the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄轉納言上士，專掌文翰，甚有美稱。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Senior Clerk in the Secretariat, exclusively in charge of documents, and won great praise.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Senior Clerk in the Secretariat, where he took charge of official documents and earned a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 加威烈將軍、員外散騎侍郎，修起居注。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed General of Majestic Power and Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier, and compiled the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed General of Majestic Power and Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier, and worked on the Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 其後襲封臨涇公。

translations.literal: Thereafter he inherited the title Duke of Linjing.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited the title of Duke of Linjing.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，轉內史下大夫，進位使持節、大將軍，儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he was transferred to Grand Master in the Inner Secretariat, and advanced to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General, with the privileges of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he was transferred to Grand Master in the Inner Secretariat and promoted to Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Grand General with the privileges of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，遷授散騎常侍、秘書監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he was transferred and appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he was appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 弘以典籍遺逸，上表請開獻書之路，曰：

translations.literal: Because the classics and records had been lost, Hong submitted a memorial asking that a path be opened for presenting books, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that many classics and records had been lost, Hong submitted a memorial requesting that the court open a channel for book donations. He wrote:

sentences.zh: 經籍所興，由來尚矣。

translations.literal: The rise of the classics and records has been esteemed from of old.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of the classics and written records has been honored since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 爻畫肇於庖羲，文字生於蒼頡。

translations.literal: The trigram lines began with Paoxi; writing was born with Cangjie.
translations.idiomatic: The trigram lines originated with Paoxi, and writing was invented by Cangjie.

sentences.zh: 聖人所以弘宣教導，博通古今，揚于王庭，肆于時夏。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages expanded teaching and guidance, mastered past and present, displayed them in the royal court, and spread them throughout the age of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The sages used them to spread teaching and guidance, to master past and present, to proclaim learning in the royal court, and to disseminate it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 故堯稱至聖，猶考古道而言；

translations.literal: Thus even Yao, called the utmost sage, still spoke by investigating the ancient Way;
translations.idiomatic: Even Yao, called the supreme sage, still spoke by studying the ways of antiquity;

sentences.zh: 舜其大智，尚觀古人之象。

translations.literal: Shun, with his great wisdom, still observed the images of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: and Shun, for all his great wisdom, still studied the symbolic models of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 《周官》外史掌三皇五帝之書，及四方之志。

translations.literal: The Outer Scribe in the Offices of Zhou was in charge of the writings of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, and of the records of the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: The Outer Scribe in the Offices of Zhou was charged with keeping the writings of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and the records of the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 武王問黃帝、顓頊之道，太公曰：「在《丹書》。」

translations.literal: King Wu asked about the Way of the Yellow Emperor and Zhuanxu, and Taigong said: "It is in the Cinnabar Book.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu asked about the Way of the Yellow Emperor and Zhuanxu, Taigong replied, "It is recorded in the Cinnabar Book.

sentences.zh: 是知握符禦曆，有國有家者，曷嘗不以《詩》、《書》而為教，因禮樂而成功也。

translations.literal: From this we know that those who hold the talisman and govern the calendar, who possess a state and a family, have never failed to take the Odes and Documents as their teaching and to achieve success through rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that every ruler who has held the mandate and governed the realm has taken the Odes and Documents as the basis of instruction and achieved success through rites and music.

sentences.zh: 昔周德既衰，舊經紊棄。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Zhou virtue had declined, the old classics were thrown into disorder and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In former times, when the virtue of Zhou had waned, the old classics fell into disorder and were cast aside.

sentences.zh: 孔子以大聖之才，開素王之業，憲章祖述，制《禮》刊《詩》，正五始而修《春秋》，闡《十翼》而弘《易》道。

translations.literal: Confucius, with the talent of a great sage, opened the enterprise of the uncrowned king, took the ancients as his model and carried on their tradition, made the Rites and edited the Odes, fixed the five beginnings and compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, expounded the Ten Wings and expanded the Way of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, with the talent of a great sage, took up the work of the uncrowned king. He modeled himself on the ancients, compiled the Rites, edited the Odes, established the five beginnings and revised the Spring and Autumn Annals, and expounded the Ten Wings to develop the Way of the Changes.

sentences.zh: 治國立身，作範垂法。

translations.literal: In governing the state and establishing the person, he set the pattern and handed down the law.
translations.idiomatic: In governing the state and ordering one's life, he set the standard and handed down the law.

sentences.zh: 及秦皇馭宇，吞滅諸侯，任用威力，事不師古，始下焚書之令，行偶語之刑。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor of Qin ruled the realm, swallowed up the feudal lords, relied on force, took no teacher from antiquity, first issued the order to burn books, and enforced the penalty for paired speech.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Emperor of Qin ruled the realm, conquered the feudal lords, and relied on brute force rather than the lessons of antiquity, he issued the order to burn books and imposed the death penalty for private discussion.

sentences.zh: 先王墳籍，掃地皆盡。

translations.literal: The tombs and records of the former kings were swept clean to the last.
translations.idiomatic: The writings of the former kings were swept away entirely.

sentences.zh: 本既先亡，從而顛覆。

translations.literal: The root was already lost first, and then came overthrow.
translations.idiomatic: The foundation was destroyed first, and collapse followed.

sentences.zh: 臣以圖讖言之，經典盛衰，信有徵數。

translations.literal: Your servant speaks by the prognostic charts: the rise and fall of the classics truly have their signs and numbers.
translations.idiomatic: If one speaks by the prognostic charts, the rise and fall of the classics truly follow a fixed pattern of signs.

sentences.zh: 此則書之一厄也。

translations.literal: This was the first calamity of books.
translations.idiomatic: This was the first great calamity for books.

sentences.zh: 漢興，改秦之弊，敦尚儒術，建藏書之策，置校書之官，屋壁山岩，往往間出。

translations.literal: When Han arose, it corrected Qin's abuses, earnestly honored Confucian learning, established policies for storing books, and appointed officials to collate texts; from house walls and mountain cliffs, texts often emerged here and there.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose, it corrected the abuses of Qin, earnestly promoted Confucian learning, established policies for collecting books, and appointed officials to collate texts. Hidden texts often emerged from house walls and mountain caves.

sentences.zh: 外有太常、太史之藏，內有延閣、秘書之府。

translations.literal: Outside were the repositories of the Grand Master of Ceremonies and the Grand Astrologer; inside were the halls of Yange and the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the court were the archives of the Grand Master of Ceremonies and the Grand Astrologer; inside were the Yange Hall and the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至孝成之世，亡逸尚多，遣謁者陳農求遺書於天下，詔劉向父子讎校篇籍。

translations.literal: By the reign of Emperor Xiaocheng, many losses still remained; he sent the usher Chen Nong to seek lost books throughout the realm, and ordered Liu Xiang and his son to collate the texts.
translations.idiomatic: By the reign of Emperor Xiaocheng, many texts were still missing. The emperor sent the usher Chen Nong to search the realm for lost books and ordered Liu Xiang and his son to collate the collections.

sentences.zh: 漢之典文，于斯為盛。

translations.literal: Han canonical writings reached their greatest abundance at this time.
translations.idiomatic: The canonical writings of Han reached their greatest abundance at this time.

sentences.zh: 及王莽之末，長安兵起，宮室圖書，並從焚燼。

translations.literal: At the end of Wang Mang's reign, armies rose in Chang'an, and the palace buildings and books all went up in flames.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wang Mang's reign, war broke out in Chang'an, and the palace buildings and books were all consumed by fire.

sentences.zh: 此則書之二厄也。

translations.literal: This was the second calamity of books.
translations.idiomatic: This was the second great calamity for books.

sentences.zh: 光武嗣興，尤重經誥，未及下車，先求文雅。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu succeeded and revived the dynasty, especially honoring the classics and edicts; before he had even stepped down from his carriage, he first sought out refined learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty, he placed special weight on the classics and edicts. Before he had even stepped down from his carriage, he began seeking out learned men.

sentences.zh: 於是鴻生巨儒，繼踵而集，懷經負帙，不遠斯至。

translations.literal: Thereupon great scholars and eminent Confucians gathered one after another, bearing classics and carrying bundles of texts, coming from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Great scholars and eminent Confucians then gathered in succession, carrying classics and bundles of texts from far and near.

sentences.zh: 肅宗親臨講肄，和帝數幸書林，其蘭台、石室，鴻都、東觀，秘牒填委，更倍於前。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong personally attended lectures, and Emperor He often visited the forest of books; at the Orchid Terrace, Stone Chamber, Hongdu, and Eastern View, secret documents piled up, more than double what had been before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong personally attended lectures, and Emperor He often visited the libraries. At the Orchid Terrace, Stone Chamber, Hongdu, and Eastern View, secret archives piled up to more than twice their former number.

sentences.zh: 及孝獻移都，吏民擾亂，圖書縑帛，皆取為帷囊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaoxian moved the capital, officials and people were thrown into disorder, and books, maps, and silk scrolls were all taken for curtains and bags.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xian moved the capital, officials and commoners fell into disorder, and books, maps, and silk scrolls were all seized for curtains and sacks.

sentences.zh: 所收而西，裁七十餘乘。

translations.literal: Of what was gathered and taken west, there were barely more than seventy cartloads.
translations.idiomatic: Of what was collected and taken west, barely more than seventy cartloads remained.

sentences.zh: 屬西京大亂，一時燔蕩。

translations.literal: Just then the Western Capital fell into great disorder, and everything was burned at once.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Western Capital fell into great disorder, and everything was burned at once.

sentences.zh: 此則書之三厄也。

translations.literal: This was the third calamity of books.
translations.idiomatic: This was the third great calamity for books.

sentences.zh: 魏文代漢，更集經典，皆藏在秘書、內外三閣，遣秘書郎鄭默刪定舊文。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei replaced Han, gathered the classics anew, and stored them all in the Secretariat and the inner and outer Three Pavilions; he sent Secretariat Gentleman Zheng Mo to revise the old texts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei replaced Han, he gathered the classics anew and stored them in the Secretariat and the inner and outer Three Pavilions. He sent Secretariat Gentleman Zheng Mo to revise the old texts.

sentences.zh: 時之論者，美其硃紫有別。

translations.literal: Commentators of the time praised him for distinguishing vermilion from purple.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators of the time praised him for clearly distinguishing authentic from spurious texts.

sentences.zh: 晉氏承之，文籍尤廣。

translations.literal: The Jin inherited this, and written records were especially extensive.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin dynasty inherited this work, and its written records became especially extensive.

sentences.zh: 晉秘書監荀勖定魏《內經》，更著《新簿》。

translations.literal: Jin Director of the Secretariat Xun Xu fixed the Wei Inner Classic and further compiled the New Catalogue.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu, Director of the Secretariat under Jin, revised the Wei Inner Classic and compiled the New Catalogue.

sentences.zh: 雖古文舊簡，猶雲有缺，新章後錄，鳩集已多，足得恢弘正道，訓範當世。

translations.literal: Although ancient texts and old bamboo slips were still said to be incomplete, newly compiled later records had already been gathered in great number, enough to expand the correct Way and provide models for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Although ancient texts and old bamboo slips were still incomplete, newly compiled works had already been gathered in great number, enough to expand the correct Way and provide models for the age.

sentences.zh: 屬劉、石憑陵，京華覆滅，朝章國典，從而失墜。

translations.literal: When Liu and Shi overran the land, the capital was destroyed, and court regulations and state statutes were lost along with it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liu and Shi regimes overran the land, the capital was destroyed, and court regulations and state statutes were lost with it.

sentences.zh: 此則書之四厄也。

translations.literal: This was the fourth calamity of books.
translations.idiomatic: This was the fourth great calamity for books.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之後，寇竊競興。

translations.literal: After the Yongjia era, bandits and usurpers rose in rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongjia era, bandits and usurpers rose one after another.

sentences.zh: 因河據洛，跨秦帶趙。

translations.literal: They held the Yellow River and occupied Luoyang, spanning Qin and embracing Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: They held the Yellow River, occupied Luoyang, and stretched across Qin and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 論其建國立家，雖傳名號，憲章禮樂，寂滅無聞。

translations.literal: Speaking of their founding states and establishing families, although they transmitted titles, their statutes, rites, and music vanished without a trace.
translations.idiomatic: For all their founding of states and dynasties, although titles were handed down, their statutes, rites, and music vanished without a trace.

sentences.zh: 劉裕平姚，收其圖籍，五經子史，才四千卷，皆赤軸青紙，文字古拙。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu pacified Yao, he collected their maps and records; the Five Classics, masters, and histories amounted to only four thousand scrolls, all with red rollers and blue paper, the characters ancient and crude.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu pacified the Yao regime, he collected its maps and records. The Five Classics, masters, and histories amounted to only four thousand scrolls, all on red rollers and blue paper, with ancient and crude characters.

sentences.zh: 僭偽之盛，莫過二秦，以此而論，足可明矣。

translations.literal: Among the flourishing of usurping regimes, none surpassed the two Qins; judged by this, the point is clear enough.
translations.idiomatic: Among the usurping regimes, none was greater than the two Qin dynasties. Judged by this, the point is clear enough.

sentences.zh: 故知衣冠軌物，圖畫記注，播遷之餘，皆歸江左。

translations.literal: Thus we know that after the scattering, robes and caps, ritual objects, paintings, records, and annotations all ended up in the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we know that after the great scattering, robes and caps, ritual objects, paintings, records, and annotations all ended up in the lands south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋之際，學藝為多，齊、梁之間，經史彌盛。

translations.literal: Between Jin and Song, learning and arts were abundant; between Qi and Liang, classics and histories flourished ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Between Jin and Song, learning and the arts flourished; between Qi and Liang, classics and histories grew ever more abundant.

sentences.zh: 宋秘書丞王儉，依劉氏《七略》，撰為《七志》。

translations.literal: Song Secretariat Assistant Wang Jian, following Liu's Seven Summaries, compiled the Seven Records.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, Assistant Director of the Song Secretariat, following Liu's Seven Summaries, compiled the Seven Records.

sentences.zh: 梁人阮孝緒，亦為《七錄》。

translations.literal: Ruan Xiaoxu of Liang also compiled the Seven Bibliographies.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xiaoxu of Liang also compiled the Seven Bibliographies.

sentences.zh: 總其書數，三萬餘卷。

translations.literal: Counting the books altogether, there were more than thirty thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether, the number of books exceeded thirty thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 及侯景渡江，破滅梁室，秘省經籍，雖從兵火，其文德殿內書史，宛然猶存。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze and destroyed the Liang house, the classics in the Secretariat were consumed by war, but the books and histories inside the Hall of Literary Virtue remained intact as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze and destroyed the Liang dynasty, the classics in the Secretariat were consumed by war, but the books and histories in the Hall of Literary Virtue remained largely intact.

sentences.zh: 蕭繹據有江陵，遣將破平侯景，收文德之書，及公私典籍，重本七萬餘卷，悉送荊州。

translations.literal: Xiao Yi held Jiangling, sent generals to defeat and pacify Hou Jing, collected the books of the Hall of Literary Virtue and public and private collections, more than seventy thousand duplicate scrolls in all, and sent them all to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi held Jiangling, sent generals to defeat Hou Jing, and collected the books of the Hall of Literary Virtue along with public and private collections—more than seventy thousand duplicate scrolls in all—and sent them to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 故江表圖書，因斯盡萃於繹矣。

translations.literal: Thus the books and maps south of the Yangtze were thereby all gathered under Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the books and maps south of the Yangtze were all gathered under Xiao Yi.

sentences.zh: 及周師入郢，繹悉焚之於外城，所收十才一二。

translations.literal: When Zhou armies entered Ying, Yi burned them all in the outer city; of what was saved, barely one or two in ten remained.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou armies entered Ying, Xiao Yi burned them all in the outer city. Of what was saved, barely one or two in ten remained.

sentences.zh: 此則書之五厄也。

translations.literal: This was the fifth calamity of books.
translations.idiomatic: This was the fifth great calamity for books.

sentences.zh: 後魏爰 自幽方，遷宅伊、洛，日不暇給，經籍闕如。

translations.literal: Later Wei came from the northern regions, moved its seat to the Yi and Luo rivers, had not a day's leisure, and its classics and records were deficient.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei came from the northern frontier and moved its capital to the Yi and Luo rivers. With not a day's leisure, its classics and records remained deficient.

sentences.zh: 周氏創基關右，戎車未息。

translations.literal: The Zhou house founded its base in the lands west of the Pass, and war chariots had not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou dynasty founded its base west of the Pass, and war chariots had not yet ceased.

sentences.zh: 保定之始，書止八千，後加收集，方盈萬卷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, books numbered only eight thousand; after further collection, they barely reached ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding, books numbered only eight thousand scrolls. After further collection, they barely reached ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 高氏據有山東，初亦採訪，驗其本目，殘缺猶多。

translations.literal: The Gao house held Shandong; at first it also searched and collected, but when the original catalogues were checked, many gaps still remained.
translations.idiomatic: The Gao regime held Shandong. At first it also searched and collected books, but when the original catalogues were checked, many gaps still remained.

sentences.zh: 及東夏初平，獲其經史，四部重雜，三萬餘卷。

translations.literal: When eastern Xia was first pacified, its classics and histories were obtained—more than thirty thousand scrolls in the four categories, many of them duplicates.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern Xia was first pacified, its classics and histories were obtained—more than thirty thousand scrolls in the four categories, many of them duplicates.

sentences.zh: 所益舊書，五千而已。

translations.literal: Of old books newly added, there were only five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Of genuinely new additions to the old collection, there were only five thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 今禦書單本，合一萬五千餘卷，部帙之間，仍有殘缺。

translations.literal: Now the imperial books in single copies total more than fifteen thousand scrolls, and among the sections and fascicles there are still gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Today the imperial collection in single copies totals more than fifteen thousand scrolls, and gaps remain among the sections and fascicles.

sentences.zh: 比梁之舊目，止有其半。

translations.literal: Compared with the old Liang catalogue, it amounts to only half.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the old Liang catalogue, it amounts to only half.

sentences.zh: 至於陰陽河洛之篇，醫方圖譜之說，彌複為少。

translations.literal: As for writings on yin and yang and the River Chart and Luo Writing, and medical formulas and illustrated treatises, they are even fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Writings on yin and yang, the River Chart and Luo Writing, medical formulas, and illustrated treatises are even scarcer.

sentences.zh: 臣以經書自仲尼已後，迄於當今，年逾千載，數遭五厄，興集之期，屬膺聖世。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that from Confucius until today, more than a thousand years have passed, and the classics have suffered the five calamities several times; the time for gathering and restoring them falls upon this sage age.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant considers that from Confucius until today, more than a thousand years have passed and the classics have suffered five great calamities. The time for gathering and restoring them has now arrived in this sage age.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下受天明命，君臨區宇，功無與二，德冠往初。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has received the bright mandate of Heaven, rules over the realm, has achievements unmatched by any second, and virtue surpassing all former beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has received Heaven's bright mandate and rules the realm. Your achievements are unmatched, and your virtue surpasses that of all former rulers.

sentences.zh: 自華夏分離，彝倫攸斁，其間雖霸王遞起，而世難未夷，欲崇儒業，時或未可。

translations.literal: Since the separation of Huaxia, the constant norms have been disrupted; although hegemons and kings rose in succession, the age's troubles were not yet settled, and to exalt Confucian learning was sometimes not yet possible.
translations.idiomatic: Since the realm was divided, the constant norms have been disrupted. Although hegemons and kings rose in succession, the troubles of the age were not yet settled, and there were times when exalting Confucian learning was not yet possible.

sentences.zh: 今土宇邁于三王，民黎盛於兩漢，有人有時，正在今日。

translations.literal: Now the territory surpasses the Three Kings, and the people flourish more than in the two Han dynasties; there are the men and there is the time—precisely today.
translations.idiomatic: Now the territory surpasses that of the Three Kings, and the people are more numerous than in the two Han dynasties. The men and the moment are both at hand—precisely today.

sentences.zh: 方當大弘文教，納俗升平，而天下圖書，尚有遺逸，非所以仰協聖情，流訓無窮者也。

translations.literal: Just as culture and teaching are to be greatly expanded and customs brought to peace, books throughout the realm still remain lost—this is not the way to accord with the sage's intent and to spread instruction without end.
translations.idiomatic: Just as culture and teaching are to be greatly expanded and the people brought to peace, books throughout the realm still remain lost. This is not the way to accord with Your Majesty's intent or to spread instruction without end.

sentences.zh: 臣史籍是司，寢興懷懼。

translations.literal: Your servant is charged with the historical records, and whether sleeping or waking I am filled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is charged with the historical records, and whether sleeping or waking I am filled with anxiety.

sentences.zh: 昔陸賈奏漢祖雲「天下不可馬上治之」，故知經邦立政，在於典謨矣。

translations.literal: Formerly Lu Jia told Emperor Gaozu of Han that "the realm cannot be governed from horseback," and thus we know that governing the state and establishing policy depend on the classics and counsels.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Lu Jia told Emperor Gaozu of Han that "the realm cannot be governed from horseback." Thus we know that governing the state and establishing policy depend on the classics and counsels.

sentences.zh: 為國之本，莫此攸先。

translations.literal: As the foundation of governing the state, nothing comes before this.
translations.idiomatic: As the foundation of governing the state, nothing comes before this.

sentences.zh: 今秘藏見書，亦足披覽，但一時載籍，須令大備。

translations.literal: The books now visible in the secret storehouses are enough for perusal, but the records of the age must be made fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: The books now in the secret archives are enough for perusal, but the records of the age must be made fully complete.

sentences.zh: 不可王府所無，私家乃有。

translations.literal: It must not be that the royal house lacks what private families possess.
translations.idiomatic: It must not be that the royal house lacks what private families possess.

sentences.zh: 然士民殷雜，求訪難知，縱有知者，多懷吝惜，必須勒之以天威，引之以微利。

translations.literal: Yet scholars and commoners are numerous and mixed; seeking and inquiring is hard to know; even if there are those who know, many harbor stinginess. They must be compelled by Heaven's majesty and drawn by small profit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet scholars and commoners are numerous and mixed, and it is hard to know where to search. Even when someone knows of a text, many are reluctant to part with it. They must be compelled by imperial authority and enticed by modest reward.

sentences.zh: 若猥發明詔，兼開購賞，則異典必臻，觀閣斯積，重道之風，超於前世，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty broadly issues a bright edict and also opens purchase and reward, then rare classics will surely arrive, the viewing halls will be filled, and the wind of honoring the Way will surpass former ages—is this not good!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty broadly issues an edict and also opens purchase and reward, then rare classics will surely arrive, the viewing halls will be filled, and the esteem for learning will surpass former ages. Would this not be excellent!

sentences.zh: 伏願天鑒，少垂照察。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly hopes Heaven's mirror will deign to cast a little light and scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly hopes that Heaven's mirror will deign to cast a little light upon this proposal.

sentences.zh: 上納之，於是下詔：獻書一卷，賚縑一匹。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it, and thereupon issued an edict: for each scroll presented, one bolt of silk was given as reward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the proposal and issued an edict: for each scroll presented, one bolt of silk was given as reward.

sentences.zh: 一二年間，篇籍稍備。

translations.literal: Within one or two years, the texts were gradually made complete.
translations.idiomatic: Within one or two years, the collections were gradually made complete.

sentences.zh: 進爵奇章郡公，邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Duke of Qizhang Commandery with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced in rank to Duke of Qizhang Commandery with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜禮部尚書，奉敕修撰《五禮》，勒成百卷，行於當世。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed Minister of Rites, received an edict to compile the Five Rites, completed one hundred scrolls, and they were practiced in the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, he was appointed Minister of Rites. By imperial order he compiled the Five Rites in one hundred scrolls, and they were put into practice in his own time.

sentences.zh: 弘請依古制修立明堂，上議曰：

translations.literal: Hong requested that the Bright Hall be built and established according to ancient institutions, and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Hong requested that the Bright Hall be built according to ancient institutions and submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 竊謂明堂者，所以通神靈，感天地，出教化，崇有德。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the Bright Hall is what communicates with spirits, moves Heaven and Earth, brings forth teaching and transformation, and honors the virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant considers that the Bright Hall is what communicates with the spirits, moves Heaven and Earth, brings forth teaching and transformation, and honors the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》曰：「宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。」

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Perform the ancestral sacrifice to King Wen in the Bright Hall, to match with the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says, "Perform the ancestral sacrifice to King Wen in the Bright Hall, to match with the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 《祭義》雲：「祀於明堂，教諸侯孝也。」

translations.literal: The Meaning of Sacrifice says: "Sacrificing in the Bright Hall teaches the feudal lords filial piety."
translations.idiomatic: The Meaning of Sacrifice says, "Sacrificing in the Bright Hall teaches the feudal lords filial piety."

sentences.zh: 黃帝曰合宮，堯曰五府，舜曰總章，布政興治，由來尚矣。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor called it the Harmonious Palace, Yao called it the Five Chambers, Shun called it the General Banner—proclaiming government and raising order has been honored from of old.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor called it the Harmonious Palace, Yao called it the Five Chambers, and Shun called it the General Banner. Proclaiming government and raising order has been honored since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 周官考工記曰：「夏后氏世室，堂脩二七，廣四脩一。」

translations.literal: The Record of Crafts in the Offices of Zhou says: "The Hall of Generations of the Xia had a hall seven times two in length, and four plus one-fourth in width.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Crafts in the Offices of Zhou says, "The Hall of Generations of the Xia had a hall fourteen units long and four and one-quarter units wide.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注云：「脩十四步，其廣益以四分脩之一，則堂廣十七步半也。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: "Seven times two is fourteen paces in length; adding one-fourth of the length to the width, the hall is seventeen and a half paces wide."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary says, "Fourteen paces in length; adding one-fourth of the length to the width, the hall is seventeen and a half paces wide."

sentences.zh: 「殷人重屋，堂脩七尋，四阿重屋。」

translations.literal: The people of Yin had a layered hall; the hall was seven xun in length, with four eaves and layered roofs.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yin had a layered hall; the hall was seven xun in length, with four eaves and layered roofs.

sentences.zh: 鄭云：「其脩七尋，廣九尋也。」

translations.literal: Zheng says: "Its length is seven xun, and its width nine xun."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng says, "Its length is seven xun, and its width nine xun."

sentences.zh: 「周人明堂，度九尺之筵，南北七筵，五室，凡室二筵。」

translations.literal: The Zhou people had the Bright Hall, measuring mats of nine chi; seven mats north and south, five chambers, each chamber two mats.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou people had the Bright Hall, measured in mats of nine chi: seven mats north and south, five chambers, each chamber two mats in size.

sentences.zh: 鄭雲：「此三者，或舉宗廟，或舉王寢，或舉明堂，互言之，明其同制也。」

translations.literal: Zheng says: "These three sometimes refer to the ancestral temple, sometimes to the king's sleeping quarters, sometimes to the Bright Hall; speaking of them interchangeably shows they share the same institution."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng says, "These three sometimes refer to the ancestral temple, sometimes to the king's sleeping quarters, and sometimes to the Bright Hall. Speaking of them interchangeably shows that they share the same institution."

sentences.zh: 馬融、王肅、幹寶所注，與鄭亦異，今不具出。

translations.literal: The commentaries of Ma Rong, Wang Su, and Gan Bao also differ from Zheng's; they are not fully set forth here.
translations.idiomatic: The commentaries of Ma Rong, Wang Su, and Gan Bao also differ from Zheng's, but they are not fully set forth here.

sentences.zh: 漢司徒馬宮議雲：「夏後氏世室，室顯於堂，故命以室。

translations.literal: Han Chancellor of State Ma Gong's memorial says: "The Hall of Generations of the Xia had chambers prominent over the hall, and so was named for chambers.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial, Han Chancellor of State Ma Gong wrote, "The Hall of Generations of the Xia had chambers that stood out from the hall, and so it was named for chambers.

sentences.zh: 殷人重屋，屋顯於堂，故命以屋。

translations.literal: The people of Yin had a layered hall; the roof structure was prominent over the hall, and so it was named for the roof.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yin had a layered hall; the roof structure stood out from the hall, and so it was named for the roof.

sentences.zh: 周人明堂，堂大於夏室，故命以堂。

translations.literal: The Zhou people had the Bright Hall; the hall was larger than the Xia chambers, and so it was named for the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou people had the Bright Hall; the hall was larger than the Xia chambers, and so it was named for the hall.

sentences.zh: 夏後氏益其堂之廣百四十四尺，周人明堂，以為兩序間大夏後氏七十二尺。」

translations.literal: The Xia added to the width of their hall one hundred forty-four chi; the Zhou Bright Hall took the space between the two side corridors of the Xia as seventy-two chi.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia added one hundred forty-four chi to the width of their hall. The Zhou Bright Hall took the space between the two side corridors of the Xia hall as seventy-two chi.

sentences.zh: 若據鄭玄之說，則夏室大於周堂，如依馬宮之言，則周堂大於夏室。

translations.literal: If one follows Zheng Xuan's explanation, the Xia chambers are larger than the Zhou hall; if one follows Ma Gong's words, the Zhou hall is larger than the Xia chambers.
translations.idiomatic: If one follows Zheng Xuan's explanation, the Xia chambers are larger than the Zhou hall; if one follows Ma Gong's words, the Zhou hall is larger than the Xia chambers.

sentences.zh: 後王轉文，周大為是。

translations.literal: Later kings turned to refined learning, and the Zhou being larger is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Later kings turned to refined learning, and the view that the Zhou hall was larger is correct.

sentences.zh: 但宮之所言，未詳其義。

translations.literal: But what Gong said is not fully explained in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: But Ma Gong's explanation is not fully clear in meaning.

sentences.zh: 此皆去聖久遠，禮文殘缺，先儒解說，家異人殊。

translations.literal: All this is far removed from the sages; ritual texts are incomplete, and the explanations of earlier Confucians differ from school to school and man to man.
translations.idiomatic: All this is far removed from the sages. Ritual texts are incomplete, and the explanations of earlier Confucians differ from school to school and scholar to scholar.

sentences.zh: 鄭注《玉藻》亦雲：「宗廟路寢，與明堂同制。」

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary on the Jade Regalia also says: "The ancestral temple and the imperial sleeping quarters share the same institution as the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentary on the Jade Regalia also says, "The ancestral temple and the imperial sleeping quarters share the same institution as the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 《王制》曰：「寢不逾廟。」

translations.literal: The Royal Regulations say: "The sleeping quarters do not exceed the temple."
translations.idiomatic: The Royal Regulations say, "The sleeping quarters do not exceed the temple in size."

sentences.zh: 明大小是同。

translations.literal: This shows that the sizes are the same.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that their sizes are the same.

sentences.zh: 今依鄭玄注，每室及堂，止有一丈八尺，四壁之外，四尺有餘。

translations.literal: Now according to Zheng Xuan's commentary, each chamber and hall is only one zhang and eight chi; beyond the four walls there is a little more than four chi.
translations.idiomatic: Now according to Zheng Xuan's commentary, each chamber and hall is only one zhang and eight chi; beyond the four walls there is a little more than four chi of space.

sentences.zh: 若以宗廟論之，祫享之時，周人旅酬六屍，並後稷為七，先公昭穆二屍，先王昭穆二屍，合十一屍，三十六主，及君北面行事於二丈之堂，愚不及此。

translations.literal: If one speaks of the ancestral temple, at the unified sacrifice the Zhou had six corpse-figures in sequence with toasts, seven including Houji; two corpse-figures for the former dukes in zhao and mu order, two for the former kings in zhao and mu order—eleven corpse-figures in all, thirty-six spirit tablets—and the ruler facing north performing rites in a hall two zhang high: this is beyond what your servant can comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: If one speaks of the ancestral temple, at the unified sacrifice the Zhou had six corpse-figures receiving toasts in sequence, seven including Houji; two corpse-figures for the former dukes in zhao and mu order and two for the former kings in the same order—eleven corpse-figures in all and thirty-six spirit tablets—and the ruler facing north performing rites in a hall only two zhang high: this is beyond what your servant can comprehend.

sentences.zh: 若以正寢論之，例須朝宴。

translations.literal: If one speaks of the principal sleeping quarters, by rule there must be court audiences and banquets.
translations.idiomatic: If one speaks of the principal sleeping quarters, by rule there must be court audiences and banquets.

sentences.zh: 據《燕禮》：「諸侯宴，則賓及卿大夫脫屨升坐。」

translations.literal: According to the Banquet Rites: "When feudal lords hold a banquet, the guest and the grand masters and grand officers remove their shoes and ascend to be seated.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Banquet Rites, "When feudal lords hold a banquet, the guest and the grandees and grand officers remove their shoes and ascend to be seated.

sentences.zh: 是知天子宴，則三公九卿並須升堂。

translations.literal: From this we know that when the Son of Heaven holds a banquet, the Three Excellencies and Nine Ministers must all ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that when the Son of Heaven holds a banquet, the Three Excellencies and Nine Ministers must all ascend the hall.

sentences.zh: 《燕義》又雲：「席，小卿次上卿。」

translations.literal: The Meaning of the Banquet also says: "In seating, the junior grand masters are next to the senior grand masters.
translations.idiomatic: The Meaning of the Banquet also says, "In seating, the junior grandees are placed next to the senior grandees.

sentences.zh: 言皆侍席。

translations.literal: This means all attend at the mats.
translations.idiomatic: This means that all attend at the mats.

sentences.zh: 止於二筵之間，豈得行禮？

translations.literal: Confined to the space of two mats, how could rites be performed?
translations.idiomatic: Confined to the space of two mats, how could rites be performed?

sentences.zh: 若以明堂論之，總享之時，五帝各於其室。

translations.literal: If one speaks of the Bright Hall, at the general sacrifice each of the Five Emperors is in his own chamber.
translations.idiomatic: If one speaks of the Bright Hall, at the general sacrifice each of the Five Emperors occupies his own chamber.

sentences.zh: 設青帝之位，須於木室之內，少北西面。

translations.literal: To set the seat of the Green Emperor, it must be inside the Wood Chamber, slightly north and facing west.
translations.idiomatic: To set the seat of the Green Emperor, it must be inside the Wood Chamber, slightly to the north and facing west.

sentences.zh: 太昊從食，坐於其西，近南北面。

translations.literal: Great Hao shares the food and sits to its west, nearly facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Great Hao shares the offering and sits to its west, nearly facing south.

sentences.zh: 祖宗配享者，又於青帝之南，稍退西面。

translations.literal: The ancestors who share the sacrifice are further south of the Green Emperor, slightly withdrawn and facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestors who share the sacrifice are placed further south of the Green Emperor, slightly withdrawn and facing west.

sentences.zh: 丈八之室，神位有三，加以簠簋籩豆，牛羊之俎，四海九州美物鹹設，複須席上升歌，出樽反坫，揖讓升降，亦以隘矣。

translations.literal: In a chamber one zhang and eight chi, there are three spirit seats; add the grain vessels, baskets, and stands, the trays of oxen and sheep, and all the fine things of the four seas and nine provinces set out; moreover there must be ascending to the mats to sing, bringing out wine jars and returning them to the stand, bowing and yielding in ascent and descent—the space is too cramped.
translations.idiomatic: In a chamber one zhang and eight chi, there are three spirit seats; add the grain vessels, baskets, and stands, the trays of oxen and sheep, and all the fine offerings of the four seas and nine provinces; moreover there must be ascending to the mats to sing, bringing out wine jars and returning them to the stand, and bowing and yielding in ascent and descent—the space is far too cramped.

sentences.zh: 據茲而說，近是不然。

translations.literal: Judged by this, the view is nearly incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by this, the view is nearly certainly wrong.

sentences.zh: 案劉向《別錄》及馬宮、蔡邕等所見，當時有《古文明堂禮》、《王居明堂禮》、《明堂圖》、《明堂大圖》、《明堂陰陽》、《太山通義》、《魏文侯孝經傳》等，並說古明堂之事。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's Separate Records and what Ma Gong, Cai Yong, and others saw, at that time there were the Ancient Text Bright Hall Rites, the King's Residence Bright Hall Rites, the Bright Hall Diagram, the Great Bright Hall Diagram, Bright Hall Yin and Yang, Mount Tai Comprehensive Meaning, and the Wei Marquis Wen Commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety, all describing matters of the ancient Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: According to Liu Xiang's Separate Records and what Ma Gong, Cai Yong, and others saw, at that time there were works such as the Ancient Text Bright Hall Rites, the King's Residence Bright Hall Rites, the Bright Hall Diagram, the Great Bright Hall Diagram, Bright Hall Yin and Yang, Mount Tai Comprehensive Meaning, and the Wei Marquis Wen Commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety, all describing matters of the ancient Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 其書皆亡，莫得而正。

translations.literal: Those books are all lost and cannot be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Those books are all lost and cannot be verified.

sentences.zh: 今《明堂月令》者，鄭玄雲：「是呂不韋著，《春秋十二紀》之首章，禮家鈔合為記。」

translations.literal: Now the Bright Hall Monthly Ordinances—Zheng Xuan says: "This was written by Lü Buwei, the opening chapter of the Twelve Annals of the Spring and Autumn, copied and assembled by ritualists into a record.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Bright Hall Monthly Ordinances, Zheng Xuan says, "This was written by Lü Buwei, the opening chapter of the Twelve Annals of the Spring and Autumn, copied and assembled by ritualists into a record.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕、王肅雲：「周公所作《周書》內有《月令》第五十三，即此也。

translations.literal: Cai Yong and Wang Su say: "Within the Book of Zhou composed by the Duke of Zhou there is the Monthly Ordinances as the fifty-third section—this is it.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong and Wang Su say, "Within the Book of Zhou composed by the Duke of Zhou there is the Monthly Ordinances as the fifty-third section—this is it.

sentences.zh: 各有證明，文多不載。

translations.literal: Each has proofs, but the texts are mostly not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Each side has proofs, but the texts are mostly not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 束皙以為夏時之書。」

translations.literal: Shu Xi considered it a book of Xia times."
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi considered it a book of Xia times."

sentences.zh: 劉獻雲：「不韋鳩集儒者，尋于聖王月令之事而記之。

translations.literal: Liu Xian says: "Lü Buwei gathered Confucians and recorded the monthly ordinances of the sage kings.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian says, "Lü Buwei gathered Confucians and recorded the monthly ordinances of the sage kings.

sentences.zh: 不韋安能獨為此記？」

translations.literal: How could Lü Buwei alone have made this record?"
translations.idiomatic: How could Lü Buwei alone have composed this record?"

sentences.zh: 今案不得全稱《周書》，亦未可即為秦典，其內雜有虞、夏、殷、周之法，皆聖王仁恕之政也。

translations.literal: Now your servant considers that it cannot wholly be called the Book of Zhou, nor can it immediately be taken as a Qin classic; within it are mixed the laws of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou—all policies of benevolence and forbearance of the sage kings.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant considers that it cannot wholly be called the Book of Zhou, nor can it immediately be taken as a Qin classic. Within it are mixed the laws of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou—all policies of benevolence and forbearance of the sage kings.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕具為章句，又論之曰：「明堂者，所以宗祀其祖以配上帝也。

translations.literal: Cai Yong fully made chapter and sentence divisions, and further discussed it, saying: "The Bright Hall is what is used to perform the ancestral sacrifice to one's forebears and match with the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong fully made chapter and sentence divisions and further discussed it, saying, "The Bright Hall is what is used to perform the ancestral sacrifice to one's forebears and match them with the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 夏後氏曰世室，殷人曰重屋，周人曰明堂。

translations.literal: The Xia called it the Hall of Generations, the Yin people called it the Layered Hall, and the Zhou people called it the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia called it the Hall of Generations, the Yin people called it the Layered Hall, and the Zhou people called it the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 東曰青陽，南曰明堂，西曰總章，北曰玄堂，內曰太室。

translations.literal: The east is called Green Yang, the south Bright Hall, the west General Banner, the north Dark Hall, and the center Great Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The east is called Green Yang, the south Bright Hall, the west General Banner, the north Dark Hall, and the center Great Chamber.

sentences.zh: 聖人南面而聽，向明而治，人君之位莫不正焉。

translations.literal: The sage faces south to listen, turns toward brightness to govern; the position of the ruler is nowhere more correct.
translations.idiomatic: The sage faces south to listen and turns toward the light to govern; nowhere is the ruler's position more correct.

sentences.zh: 故雖有五名，而主以明堂也。

translations.literal: Thus although there are five names, Bright Hall is taken as the principal.
translations.idiomatic: Thus although there are five names, Bright Hall is taken as the principal name.

sentences.zh: 制度之數，各有所依。

translations.literal: The numbers of the institution each have their basis.
translations.idiomatic: The numbers of the institution each have their basis.

sentences.zh: 堂方一百四十四尺，坤之策也，屋圓楣徑二百一十六尺，乾之策也。

translations.literal: The hall is one hundred forty-four chi square—the number of Kun; the round roof beam has a diameter of two hundred sixteen chi—the number of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: The hall is one hundred forty-four chi square—the number of Kun; the round roof beam has a diameter of two hundred sixteen chi—the number of Qian.

sentences.zh: 太廟明堂方六丈，通天屋徑九丈，陰陽九六之變，且圓蓋方覆，九六之道也。

translations.literal: The Great Temple and Bright Hall are six zhang square; the roof reaching Heaven has a diameter of nine zhang—the transformation of yin and yang's nine and six; moreover the round cover and square foundation are the Way of nine and six.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Temple and Bright Hall are six zhang square; the roof reaching Heaven has a diameter of nine zhang—the transformation of yin and yang's nine and six. The round cover and square foundation embody the Way of nine and six.

sentences.zh: 八闥以象卦，九室以象州，十二宮以應日辰。

translations.literal: Eight doorways symbolize the trigrams; nine chambers symbolize the provinces; twelve palaces correspond to the days and hours.
translations.idiomatic: Eight doorways symbolize the trigrams; nine chambers symbolize the provinces; and twelve palaces correspond to the days and hours.

sentences.zh: 三十六戶，七十二牖，以四戶八牖乘九宮之數也。

translations.literal: Thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows—four doors and eight windows multiplied by the number of the nine palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows—four doors and eight windows multiplied by the number of the nine palaces.

sentences.zh: 戶皆外設而不閉，示天下以不藏也。

translations.literal: All doors are set outward and not closed, showing the realm that nothing is hidden.
translations.idiomatic: All doors are set outward and not closed, showing the realm that nothing is hidden.

sentences.zh: 通天屋高八十一尺，黃鐘九九之實也。

translations.literal: The roof reaching Heaven is eighty-one chi high—the product of nine times nine of the Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: The roof reaching Heaven is eighty-one chi high—the product of nine times nine of the Yellow Bell pitch.

sentences.zh: 二十八柱布四方，四方七宿之象也。

translations.literal: Twenty-eight pillars are distributed in the four directions—the image of the seven lodges in each direction.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-eight pillars are distributed in the four directions—the image of the seven lodges in each direction.

sentences.zh: 堂高三尺，以應三統，四向五色，各象其行。

translations.literal: The hall is three chi high, corresponding to the three systems; the four directions and five colors each symbolize their phases.
translations.idiomatic: The hall is three chi high, corresponding to the three systems; the four directions and five colors each symbolize their phases.

sentences.zh: 水闊二十四丈，象二十四氣，於外以象四海。

translations.literal: The water is twenty-four zhang wide, symbolizing the twenty-four qi; on the outside it symbolizes the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: The water is twenty-four zhang wide, symbolizing the twenty-four seasonal nodes; on the outside it symbolizes the four seas.

sentences.zh: 王者之大禮也。」

translations.literal: This is the great rite of the king.
translations.idiomatic: This is the great rite of the king.

sentences.zh: 觀其模範天地，則象陰陽，必據古文，義不虛出。

translations.literal: Observing that it models Heaven and Earth and symbolizes yin and yang, it must be based on ancient texts; the meaning does not arise empty.
translations.idiomatic: Observing that it models Heaven and Earth and symbolizes yin and yang, it must be based on ancient texts; its meaning does not arise without foundation.

sentences.zh: 今若直取《考工》，不參《月令》，青陽總章之號不得而稱，九月享帝之禮不得而用。

translations.literal: Now if one takes only the Record of Crafts and does not consult the Monthly Ordinances, the names Green Yang and General Banner cannot be used, and the rite of sacrificing to the Emperor in the ninth month cannot be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Now if one takes only the Record of Crafts and does not consult the Monthly Ordinances, the names Green Yang and General Banner cannot be used, and the rite of sacrificing to the Emperor in the ninth month cannot be performed.

sentences.zh: 漢代二京所建，與此說悉同。

translations.literal: What was built in the two capitals of Han accorded entirely with this explanation.
translations.idiomatic: What was built in the two capitals of Han accorded entirely with this explanation.

sentences.zh: 建安之後，海內大亂，京邑焚燒，憲章泯絕。

translations.literal: After the Jian'an era, the realm fell into great disorder, the capital was burned, and statutes and regulations were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jian'an era, the realm fell into great disorder, the capital was burned, and statutes and regulations were lost.

sentences.zh: 魏氏三方未平，無聞興造。

translations.literal: The Wei house had not yet pacified the three regions, and nothing was heard of construction.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei house had not yet pacified the three regions, and nothing was heard of new construction.

sentences.zh: 晉則侍中裴頠議曰：「尊祖配天，其義明著，而廟宇之制，理據未分。

translations.literal: Under Jin, Attendant-in-Ordinary Pei Wei memorialized, saying: "Honoring the ancestors and matching Heaven—the meaning is clear; but the institution of temple buildings, its principles and evidence, are not yet distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin, Attendant-in-Ordinary Pei Wei memorialized, saying, "Honoring the ancestors and matching Heaven—the meaning is clear; but the institution of temple buildings, its principles and evidence, are not yet distinguished.

sentences.zh: 宜可直為一殿，以崇嚴父之祀，其餘雜碎，一皆除之。」

translations.literal: It would be fitting to make simply one hall, to exalt the sacrifice to the honored father; all the rest, miscellaneous and fragmentary, should be entirely removed.
translations.idiomatic: It would be fitting to make simply one hall to exalt the sacrifice to the honored father; all the rest, miscellaneous and fragmentary, should be entirely removed.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊已還，鹹率茲禮。

translations.literal: From Song and Qi onward, all followed this rite.
translations.idiomatic: From Song and Qi onward, all followed this rite.

sentences.zh: 此乃世之通儒，時無思術，前王盛事，於是不行。

translations.literal: These were the universal Confucians of the age; the times lacked thoughtful methods, and the great affairs of former kings were thereby not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: These were the universal Confucians of the age. The times lacked thoughtful methods, and the great affairs of former kings were thereby not carried out.

sentences.zh: 後魏代都所造，出自李沖，三三相重，合為九室。

translations.literal: What was built at the capital of Later Wei came from Li Chong: three by three layered together, making nine chambers in all.
translations.idiomatic: What was built at the capital of Later Wei came from Li Chong: three by three layered together, making nine chambers in all.

sentences.zh: 簷不覆基，房間通街，穿鑿處多，迄無可取。

translations.literal: The eaves did not cover the foundation; rooms opened onto streets; there were many drilled and carved places—nothing in it was acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The eaves did not cover the foundation; rooms opened onto streets; there were many drilled and carved places—nothing in it was acceptable.

sentences.zh: 及遷宅洛陽，更加營構，五九紛競，遂至不成，宗配之事，於焉靡托。

translations.literal: When they moved the seat to Luoyang, they further undertook construction; disputes over five chambers and nine chambers arose, and in the end it was not completed; the affairs of ancestral sacrifice and matching had nowhere to rest.
translations.idiomatic: When they moved the capital to Luoyang, they further undertook construction. Disputes over five chambers and nine chambers arose, and in the end it was not completed; the affairs of ancestral sacrifice and matching had nowhere to rest.

sentences.zh: 今皇猷遐闡，化覃海外，方建大禮，垂之無窮。

translations.literal: Now the imperial plan extends far; transformation reaches beyond the seas; great rites are about to be established and handed down without end.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial plan extends far, and transformation reaches beyond the seas. Great rites are about to be established and handed down without end.

sentences.zh: 弘等不以庸虛，謬當議限。

translations.literal: Hong and others, though unworthy and empty, have wrongly been placed within the limits of deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and others, though unworthy, have been placed within the limits of deliberation.

sentences.zh: 今檢明堂必須五室者何？

translations.literal: Now, examining why the Bright Hall must have five chambers:
translations.idiomatic: Now, examining why the Bright Hall must have five chambers:

sentences.zh: 《尚書帝命驗》曰：「帝者承天立五府，赤曰文祖，黃曰神鬥，白曰顯紀，黑曰玄矩，蒼曰靈府。」

translations.literal: The Verification of the Emperor's Mandate in the Book of Documents says: "The emperor, receiving Heaven, establishes five chambers: the red is called Literary Ancestor, the yellow Spirit Dipper, the white Manifest Record, the black Dark Rule, and the green Spirit Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: The Verification of the Emperor's Mandate in the Book of Documents says, "The emperor, receiving Heaven, establishes five chambers: the red is called Literary Ancestor, the yellow Spirit Dipper, the white Manifest Record, the black Dark Rule, and the green Spirit Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注曰：「五府與周之明堂同矣。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: "The five chambers are the same as the Zhou Bright Hall."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary says, "The five chambers are the same as the Zhou Bright Hall."

sentences.zh: 且三代相沿，多有損益，至於五室，確然不變。

translations.literal: Moreover, the three dynasties followed one another with many additions and subtractions; as for five chambers, they remained certainly unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the three dynasties followed one another with many additions and subtractions; as for five chambers, they remained certainly unchanged.

sentences.zh: 夫室以祭天，天實有五，若立九室，四無所用。

translations.literal: Chambers are for sacrificing to Heaven; Heaven truly has five; if nine chambers are established, four are useless.
translations.idiomatic: Chambers are for sacrificing to Heaven, and Heaven truly has five aspects. If nine chambers are established, four are useless.

sentences.zh: 布政視朔，自依其辰。

translations.literal: Proclaiming government and observing the new moon each follow their own season.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaiming government and observing the new moon each follow their own season.

sentences.zh: 鄭司農雲：「十二月分在青陽等左右之位。」

translations.literal: Zheng the Minister of Agriculture says: "The twelve months are distributed in the positions to the left and right of Green Yang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng the Minister of Agriculture says, "The twelve months are distributed in the positions to the left and right of Green Yang and the others.

sentences.zh: 不雲居室。

translations.literal: He does not speak of dwelling chambers.
translations.idiomatic: He does not speak of dwelling chambers.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄亦言：「每月于其時之堂而聽政焉。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan also says: "Each month the ruler hears government affairs in the hall of that season.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan also says, "Each month the ruler hears government affairs in the hall of that season.

sentences.zh: 《禮圖》畫個，皆在堂偏，是以須為五室。

translations.literal: The Ritual Diagrams depict figures all at the sides of the hall; therefore five chambers are required.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Diagrams depict figures all at the sides of the hall; therefore five chambers are required.

sentences.zh: 明堂必須上圓下方者何？

translations.literal: Why must the Bright Hall be round above and square below?
translations.idiomatic: Why must the Bright Hall be round above and square below?

sentences.zh: 《孝經援神契》曰：「明堂者，上圓下方，八窗四達，布政之宮。」

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety's Aid to the Spirit Covenant says: "The Bright Hall is round above and square below, with eight windows opening in four directions—the palace for proclaiming government.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety's Aid to the Spirit Covenant says, "The Bright Hall is round above and square below, with eight windows opening in four directions—the palace for proclaiming government.

sentences.zh: 《禮記·盛德篇》曰：「明堂四戶八牖，上圓下方。」

translations.literal: The chapter on Abundant Virtue in the Record of Rites says: "The Bright Hall has four doors and eight windows, round above and square below."
translations.idiomatic: The chapter on Abundant Virtue in the Record of Rites says, "The Bright Hall has four doors and eight windows, round above and square below."

sentences.zh: 《五經異義》稱講學大夫淳于登亦雲：「上圓下方。」

translations.literal: The Dissenting Opinions on the Five Classics says Lecturer Chunyu Deng also said: "Round above and square below."
translations.idiomatic: The Dissenting Opinions on the Five Classics says Lecturer Chunyu Deng also said, "Round above and square below."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄同之。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 是以須為圓方。

translations.literal: Therefore it must be round and square.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it must be round above and square below.

sentences.zh: 明堂必須重屋者何？

translations.literal: Why must the Bright Hall have layered roofs?
translations.idiomatic: Why must the Bright Hall have layered roofs?

sentences.zh: 案《考工記》，夏言「九階，四旁兩夾窗，門堂三之二，室三之一。」

translations.literal: According to the Record of Crafts, the Xia speak of "nine steps, windows flanking on four sides, the gate hall two-thirds, the chambers one-third.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Record of Crafts, the Xia speak of "nine steps, windows flanking on four sides, the gate hall two-thirds, the chambers one-third.

sentences.zh: 殷、周不言者，明一同夏制。

translations.literal: Yin and Zhou do not speak of it, showing clearly that they shared the Xia institution.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Zhou do not speak of it, showing clearly that they shared the Xia institution.

sentences.zh: 殷言「四阿重屋」，周承其後不言屋，制亦盡同可知也。」

translations.literal: Yin speaks of "four eaves and layered roofs"; Zhou inherited afterward and does not speak of roofs—the institution is entirely the same, as can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Yin speaks of "four eaves and layered roofs." Zhou inherited afterward and does not speak of roofs—the institution is entirely the same, as can be known.

sentences.zh: 其「殷人重屋」之下，本無五室之文，鄭注雲：「五室者，亦據夏以知之。」

translations.literal: Below "the Yin people had layered halls" there is originally no text about five chambers; Zheng's commentary says: "The five chambers are also known by reference to the Xia."
translations.idiomatic: Below "the Yin people had layered halls" there is originally no text about five chambers. Zheng's commentary says, "The five chambers are also known by reference to the Xia."

sentences.zh: 明周不雲重屋，因殷則有，灼然可見。

translations.literal: This shows that Zhou does not speak of layered roofs, but because Yin had them, it is clearly visible.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that although Zhou does not speak of layered roofs, because Yin had them, the point is clearly visible.

sentences.zh: 《禮記·明堂位》曰：「太廟天子明堂。」

translations.literal: The Bright Hall Position in the Record of Rites says: "The Great Temple is the Son of Heaven's Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall Position in the Record of Rites says, "The Great Temple is the Son of Heaven's Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 言魯為周公之故，得用天子禮樂，魯之太廟與周之明堂同。

translations.literal: This means that because of the Duke of Zhou, Lu was allowed to use the Son of Heaven's rites and music; Lu's Great Temple is the same as Zhou's Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: This means that because of the Duke of Zhou, Lu was allowed to use the Son of Heaven's rites and music. Lu's Great Temple is the same as Zhou's Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「複廟重簷，刮楹達向，天子之廟飾。」

translations.literal: It also says: "Double temple and layered eaves, planed pillars reaching the direction—the ornament of the Son of Heaven's temple.
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Double temple and layered eaves, planed pillars reaching the direction—the ornament of the Son of Heaven's temple.

sentences.zh: 鄭注：「複廟，重屋也。」

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary: "Double temple means layered roofs."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentary says, "Double temple means layered roofs."

sentences.zh: 據廟既重屋，明堂亦不疑矣。

translations.literal: Since the temple has layered roofs, the Bright Hall is also beyond doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Since the temple has layered roofs, the Bright Hall also certainly has them.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》文公十三年：「太室屋壞。」

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals, thirteenth year of Duke Wen: "The roof of the Great Chamber collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals, thirteenth year of Duke Wen, records, "The roof of the Great Chamber collapsed.

sentences.zh: 《五行志》曰：「前堂曰太廟，中央曰太室，屋其上重者也。」

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Five Phases says: "The front hall is called the Great Temple; the center is called the Great Chamber—the roof above it is the layered one."
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Five Phases says, "The front hall is called the Great Temple; the center is called the Great Chamber—the roof above it is the layered one."

sentences.zh: 服虔亦雲：「太室，太廟太室之上屋也。」

translations.literal: Fu Qian also says: "The Great Chamber is the roof above the Great Temple's Great Chamber."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian also says, "The Great Chamber is the roof above the Great Temple's Great Chamber."

sentences.zh: 《周書·作洛篇》曰：「乃立太廟宗宮路寢明堂，咸有四阿反坫，重亢重廊。」

translations.literal: The chapter on Building Luo in the Book of Zhou says: "Then they established the Great Temple, Ancestral Palace, Road Sleeping Quarters, and Bright Hall—all had four eaves, wine stands, layered ridgepoles, and layered corridors."
translations.idiomatic: The chapter on Building Luo in the Book of Zhou says, "Then they established the Great Temple, Ancestral Palace, Road Sleeping Quarters, and Bright Hall—all had four eaves, wine stands, layered ridgepoles, and layered corridors."

sentences.zh: 孔晁注曰：「重亢累棟，重廊累屋也。」

translations.literal: Kong Chao's commentary says: "Layered ridgepoles are accumulated beams; layered corridors are accumulated roofs."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chao's commentary says, "Layered ridgepoles are accumulated beams; layered corridors are accumulated roofs."

sentences.zh: 依《黃圖》所載，漢之宗廟皆為重屋。

translations.literal: According to what is recorded in the Yellow Diagram, all the ancestral temples of Han had layered roofs.
translations.idiomatic: According to what is recorded in the Yellow Diagram, all the ancestral temples of Han had layered roofs.

sentences.zh: 此去古猶近，遺法尚在，是以須為重屋。

translations.literal: This is still close to antiquity; the surviving institutions remain; therefore layered roofs are required.
translations.idiomatic: This is still close to antiquity, and the surviving institutions remain. Therefore layered roofs are required.

sentences.zh: 明堂必須為辟雍者何？

translations.literal: Why must the Bright Hall have a Bi Yong?
translations.idiomatic: Why must the Bright Hall have a Bi Yong enclosure?

sentences.zh: 《禮記·盛德篇》雲：「明堂者，明諸侯尊卑也。

translations.literal: The chapter on Abundant Virtue in the Record of Rites says: "The Bright Hall makes clear the precedence of the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: The chapter on Abundant Virtue in the Record of Rites says, "The Bright Hall makes clear the precedence of the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 外水曰辟雍。」

translations.literal: The outer water is called Bi Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The outer water is called Bi Yong.

sentences.zh: 《明堂陰陽錄》曰：「明堂之制，周圜行水，左旋以象天，內有太室以象紫宮。」

translations.literal: The Record of Bright Hall Yin and Yang says: "The institution of the Bright Hall has water circling round, turning left to symbolize Heaven; within is the Great Chamber to symbolize the Purple Palace."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Bright Hall Yin and Yang says, "The institution of the Bright Hall has water circling round, turning left to symbolize Heaven. Within is the Great Chamber to symbolize the Purple Palace."

sentences.zh: 此明堂有水之明文也。

translations.literal: This is explicit text that the Bright Hall has water.
translations.idiomatic: This is explicit text that the Bright Hall has water.

sentences.zh: 然馬宮、王肅以為明堂、辟雍、太學同處，蔡邕、盧植亦以為明堂、靈台、辟雍、太學同實異名。

translations.literal: Yet Ma Gong and Wang Su considered the Bright Hall, Bi Yong, and Imperial Academy to be in the same place; Cai Yong and Lu Zhi also considered the Bright Hall, Spirit Terrace, Bi Yong, and Imperial Academy to be the same reality with different names.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ma Gong and Wang Su considered the Bright Hall, Bi Yong, and Imperial Academy to occupy the same place. Cai Yong and Lu Zhi also considered the Bright Hall, Spirit Terrace, Bi Yong, and Imperial Academy to be the same institution under different names.

sentences.zh: 邕雲：「明堂者，取其宗祀之清貌，則謂之清廟，取其正室，則曰太室，取其堂，則曰明堂，取其四門之學，則曰太學，取其周水圜如璧，則曰璧雍。

translations.literal: Cai Yong says: "The Bright Hall—taking its pure aspect for ancestral sacrifice, it is called the Pure Temple; taking its principal chamber, it is called the Great Chamber; taking its hall, it is called the Bright Hall; taking its four-gate academy, it is called the Imperial Academy; taking its encircling water round like a jade disk, it is called Bi Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong says, "The Bright Hall—taking its pure aspect for ancestral sacrifice, it is called the Pure Temple; taking its principal chamber, it is called the Great Chamber; taking its hall, it is called the Bright Hall; taking its four-gate academy, it is called the Imperial Academy; taking its encircling water round like a jade disk, it is called Bi Yong.

sentences.zh: 其實一也。」

translations.literal: In reality it is one.
translations.idiomatic: In reality it is one institution.

sentences.zh: 其言別者，《五經通義》曰：「靈台以望氣，明堂以布政，辟雍以養老教學。」

translations.literal: Those who speak of them as separate—the Comprehensive Meaning of the Five Classics says: "The Spirit Terrace is for observing qi; the Bright Hall is for proclaiming government; the Bi Yong is for honoring the aged and teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Those who speak of them as separate—the Comprehensive Meaning of the Five Classics says, "The Spirit Terrace is for observing qi; the Bright Hall is for proclaiming government; the Bi Yong is for honoring the aged and teaching."

sentences.zh: 三者不同。

translations.literal: The three are different.
translations.idiomatic: The three are different.

sentences.zh: 袁準、鄭玄亦以為別。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhun and Zheng Xuan also considered them separate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhun and Zheng Xuan also considered them separate.

sentences.zh: 歷代所疑，豈能輒定？

translations.literal: What generations have doubted—how can it be settled hastily?
translations.idiomatic: What generations have doubted—how can it be settled hastily?

sentences.zh: 今據《郊祀志》雲：「欲治明堂，未曉其制。

translations.literal: Now according to the Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices: "Wishing to build the Bright Hall, they did not understand its institution.
translations.idiomatic: Now according to the Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices, "Wishing to build the Bright Hall, they did not understand its institution.

sentences.zh: 濟南人公玉帶上黃帝時《明堂圖》，一殿無壁，蓋之以 茅，水圜宮垣，天子從之。」

translations.literal: Gong Yudai of Jinan presented the Bright Hall Diagram from the time of the Yellow Emperor: one hall without walls, covered with thatch, water circling the palace walls—and the Son of Heaven followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Yudai of Jinan presented the Bright Hall Diagram from the time of the Yellow Emperor: one hall without walls, covered with thatch, with water circling the palace walls—and the Son of Heaven followed it.

sentences.zh: 以此而言，其來則久。

translations.literal: Judged by this, its origin is long.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by this, its origin is ancient.

sentences.zh: 漢中元二年，起明堂、辟雍、靈台於洛陽，並別處。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongyuan of Han, the Bright Hall, Bi Yong, and Spirit Terrace were built in Luoyang, each in a separate place.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongyuan of Han, the Bright Hall, Bi Yong, and Spirit Terrace were built in Luoyang, each in a separate location.

sentences.zh: 然明堂亦有壁水，李尤《明堂銘》雲「流水洋洋」是也。

translations.literal: Yet the Bright Hall also had encircling water; Li You's Bright Hall Inscription says "flowing water vast and wide"—this is it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Bright Hall also had encircling water. Li You's Bright Hall Inscription says "flowing water vast and wide"—this is the evidence.

sentences.zh: 以此須有辟雍。

translations.literal: For this reason a Bi Yong is required.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason a Bi Yong is required.

sentences.zh: 夫帝王作事，必師古昔，今造明堂，須以《禮經》為本。

translations.literal: When emperors and kings undertake affairs, they must take antiquity as their teacher; in building the Bright Hall now, the Ritual Classics must be taken as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: When emperors and kings undertake affairs, they must take antiquity as their teacher. In building the Bright Hall now, the Ritual Classics must be taken as the foundation.

sentences.zh: 形制依于周法，度數取於《月令》，遺闕之處，參以餘書，庶使該詳沿革之理。

translations.literal: The form and institution should follow Zhou law; measurements should be taken from the Monthly Ordinances; where there are gaps, other books should be consulted, so that the principles of evolution may be fully detailed.
translations.idiomatic: The form and institution should follow Zhou law; measurements should be taken from the Monthly Ordinances; where there are gaps, other books should be consulted, so that the principles of evolution may be fully detailed.

sentences.zh: 其五室九階，上圓下方，四阿重屋，四旁兩門，依《考工記》、《孝經》說。

translations.literal: Its five chambers and nine steps, round above and square below, four eaves and layered roofs, two doors on four sides—follow the explanations in the Record of Crafts and the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: Its five chambers and nine steps, round above and square below, four eaves and layered roofs, and two doors on four sides should follow the explanations in the Record of Crafts and the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 堂方一百四十四尺，屋圓楣徑二百一十六尺，太室方六丈，通天屋徑九丈，八達二十八柱，堂高三尺，四向五色，依《周書·月令》論。

translations.literal: The hall one hundred forty-four chi square, the round roof beam two hundred sixteen chi in diameter, the Great Chamber six zhang square, the roof reaching Heaven nine zhang in diameter, eight openings and twenty-eight pillars, the hall three chi high, four directions and five colors—follow the discussion in the Monthly Ordinances of the Book of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The hall one hundred forty-four chi square, the round roof beam two hundred sixteen chi in diameter, the Great Chamber six zhang square, the roof reaching Heaven nine zhang in diameter, eight openings and twenty-eight pillars, the hall three chi high, and four directions with five colors should follow the discussion in the Monthly Ordinances of the Book of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 殿垣方在內，水周如外，水內徑三百步，依《太山盛德記》、《覲禮經》。

translations.literal: The palace wall square within, water circling without, the inner diameter of the water three hundred paces—follow the Record of Mount Tai's Abundant Virtue and the Classic of the Tribute of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The palace wall square within, water circling without, and the inner diameter of the water three hundred paces should follow the Record of Mount Tai's Abundant Virtue and the Classic of the Tribute of Yu.

sentences.zh: 仰觀俯察，皆有則象，足以盡誠上帝，祗配祖宗，弘風布教，作范於後矣。

translations.literal: Looking up and looking down, all have their models and symbols, enough to express full sincerity to the Supreme Lord, reverently match the ancestors, spread the wind and disseminate teaching, and set the pattern for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up and looking down, all have their models and symbols, enough to express full sincerity to the Supreme Lord, reverently match the ancestors, spread culture and disseminate teaching, and set the pattern for posterity.

sentences.zh: 弘等學不稽古，輒申所見，可否之宜，伏聽裁擇。

translations.literal: Hong and others, whose learning does not investigate antiquity, presumptuously state what they have seen; whether it is suitable or not, your servant humbly awaits Your Majesty's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and others, whose learning does not fully investigate antiquity, presumptuously state what they have seen. Whether it is suitable or not, your servant humbly awaits Your Majesty's decision.

sentences.zh: 上以時事草創，未遑製作，竟寢不行。

translations.literal: The emperor, because affairs of state were still being established, had no leisure for construction, and in the end the plan was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because affairs of state were still being established, had no leisure for construction, and in the end the plan was shelved and not carried out.

sentences.zh: 六年，除太常卿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔改定雅樂，又作樂府歌詞，撰定圓丘五帝凱樂，並議樂事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, an edict ordered the revision of court music; he also composed Music Bureau lyrics, compiled the victory music for the Round Altar and Five Emperors, and deliberated on musical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, an edict ordered the revision of court music. He also composed Music Bureau lyrics, compiled the victory music for the Round Altar and Five Emperors, and deliberated on musical affairs.

sentences.zh: 弘上議雲：

translations.literal: Hong submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Hong submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 謹案《禮》，五聲、六律、十二管還相為宮。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully considers the Rites: the five tones, six pitch-standards, and twelve tubes cyclically generate one another as the tonic.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully considers the Rites: the five tones, six pitch-standards, and twelve tubes cyclically generate one another as the tonic.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》奏黃鐘，歌大呂，奏太簇，歌應鐘，皆是旋相為宮之義。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: play the Yellow Bell, sing the Great Mould; play the Great Cluster, sing the Responding Bell—all are the meaning of cyclically generating the tonic.
