translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou says to play the Yellow Bell and sing the Great Mould, play the Great Cluster and sing the Responding Bell—all embody the principle of cyclically generating the tonic.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕《明堂月令章句》曰：「孟春月則太簇為宮，姑洗為商，蕤賓為角，南呂為徵，應鐘為羽，大呂為變宮，夷則為變徵。

translations.literal: Cai Yong's chapter and sentence divisions on the Bright Hall Monthly Ordinances say: "In the first month of spring, the Great Cluster is the tonic, Maiden Wash is the second, Luxuriant Guest is the third, Southern Pitch is the fourth, Responding Bell is the fifth, Great Mould is the altered tonic, and Barren Rule is the altered fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong's chapter and sentence divisions on the Bright Hall Monthly Ordinances say, "In the first month of spring, the Great Cluster is the tonic, Maiden Wash is the second, Luxuriant Guest is the third, Southern Pitch is the fourth, Responding Bell is the fifth, Great Mould is the altered tonic, and Barren Rule is the altered fourth.

sentences.zh: 他月放此。」

translations.literal: Other months follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Other months follow this pattern.

sentences.zh: 故先王之作律呂也，所以辯天地四方陰陽之聲。

translations.literal: Therefore when the former kings made the pitch-standards, it was to distinguish the sounds of Heaven and Earth, the four directions, yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the former kings made the pitch-standards, it was to distinguish the sounds of Heaven and Earth, the four directions, and yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 揚子雲曰：「聲生於律，律生於辰。」

translations.literal: Yang Ziyun says: "Sound is born from pitch-standards; pitch-standards are born from the hours.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ziyun says, "Sound is born from pitch-standards; pitch-standards are born from the hours.

sentences.zh: 故律呂配五行，通八風，曆十二辰，行十二月，迴圈轉運，義無停止。

translations.literal: Therefore the pitch-standards match the five phases, penetrate the eight winds, pass through the twelve hours, move through the twelve months, turning in cycles without cease in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the pitch-standards match the five phases, penetrate the eight winds, pass through the twelve hours, and move through the twelve months, turning in cycles without cease.

sentences.zh: 譬如立春木王火相，立夏火王土相，季夏餘分，土王金相，立秋金王水相，立冬水王木相。

translations.literal: For example, at the Beginning of Spring wood is king and fire is minister; at the Beginning of Summer fire is king and earth is minister; in the last month of summer the remainder is divided, earth is king and metal is minister; at the Beginning of Autumn metal is king and water is minister; at the Beginning of Winter water is king and wood is minister.
translations.idiomatic: For example, at the Beginning of Spring wood is dominant and fire is secondary; at the Beginning of Summer fire is dominant and earth is secondary; in the last month of summer earth is dominant and metal is secondary; at the Beginning of Autumn metal is dominant and water is secondary; at the Beginning of Winter water is dominant and wood is secondary.

sentences.zh: 還相為宮者，謂當其王月，名之為宮。

translations.literal: Cyclically generating the tonic means that in the month when a phase is king, it is named the tonic.
translations.idiomatic: Cyclically generating the tonic means that in the month when a phase is dominant, it is named the tonic.

sentences.zh: 今若十一月不以黃鐘為宮，十三月不乙太簇為宮，便是春木不王，夏王不相，豈不陰陽失度，天地不通哉？

translations.literal: Now if in the eleventh month the Yellow Bell is not taken as the tonic, and in the thirteenth month the Great Cluster is not taken as the tonic, then spring wood is not king and summer's king has no minister—would not yin and yang lose their measure and Heaven and Earth fail to communicate?
translations.idiomatic: Now if in the eleventh month the Yellow Bell is not taken as the tonic, and in the thirteenth month the Great Cluster is not taken as the tonic, then spring wood is not dominant and summer's dominant phase has no secondary—would not yin and yang lose their measure and Heaven and Earth fail to communicate?

sentences.zh: 劉歆《鐘律書》雲：「春宮秋律，百卉必凋；

translations.literal: Liu Xin's Treatise on Bells and Pitch-Standards says: "Spring tonic with autumn pitch-standards—all plants will wither;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin's Treatise on Bells and Pitch-Standards says, "A spring tonic with autumn pitch-standards—all plants will wither;

sentences.zh: 秋宮春律，萬物必榮；

translations.literal: autumn tonic with spring pitch-standards—all things will flourish;
translations.idiomatic: an autumn tonic with spring pitch-standards—all things will flourish;

sentences.zh: 夏宮冬律，雨雹必降；

translations.literal: summer tonic with winter pitch-standards—rain and hail will surely fall;
translations.idiomatic: a summer tonic with winter pitch-standards—rain and hail will surely fall;

sentences.zh: 冬宮夏律，雷必發聲。」

translations.literal: winter tonic with summer pitch-standards—thunder will surely sound.
translations.idiomatic: a winter tonic with summer pitch-standards—thunder will surely sound.

sentences.zh: 以斯而論，誠為不易。

translations.literal: Judged by this, it is truly not to be changed lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by this, the principle is truly not to be changed lightly.

sentences.zh: 且律十二，今直為黃鐘一均，唯用七律，以外五律，竟複何施？

translations.literal: Moreover there are twelve pitch-standards; now only the Yellow Bell key is used, employing only seven standards—what use are the remaining five?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover there are twelve pitch-standards, yet now only the Yellow Bell key is used, employing only seven standards. What use are the remaining five?

sentences.zh: 恐失聖人製作本意。

translations.literal: I fear this loses the original intent of the sages' creation.
translations.idiomatic: I fear this loses the original intent of the sages' creation.

sentences.zh: 故須依禮作還相為宮之法。

translations.literal: Therefore the method of cyclically generating the tonic must be made according to the Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the method of cyclically generating the tonic must be established according to the Rites.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「不須作旋相為宮，且作黃鐘一均也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "There is no need to make cyclically generating the tonic; for now use only the Yellow Bell key.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "There is no need to make cyclically generating the tonic. For now use only the Yellow Bell key.

sentences.zh: 弘又論六十律不可行：

translations.literal: Hong further argued that the sixty pitch-standards could not be implemented:
translations.idiomatic: Hong further argued that the sixty pitch-standards could not be implemented:

sentences.zh: 謹案《續漢書·律曆志》，元帝遣韋玄成問京房于樂府，房對：「受學故小黃令焦延壽。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully considers the Treatise on Pitch-Standards and the Calendar in the Continuation of the Book of Han: Emperor Yuan sent Wei Xuancheng to question Jing Fang at the Music Bureau, and Fang replied: "I received instruction from the former Magistrate of Xiaohuang, Jiao Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully considers the Treatise on Pitch-Standards and the Calendar in the Continuation of the Book of Han: Emperor Yuan sent Wei Xuancheng to question Jing Fang at the Music Bureau, and Fang replied, "I received instruction from the former Magistrate of Xiaohuang, Jiao Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 六十律相生之法，以上生下，皆三生二，以下生上，皆三生四。

translations.literal: The method by which the sixty pitch-standards generate one another: generating downward from above, all are three generating two; generating upward from below, all are three generating four.
translations.idiomatic: The method by which the sixty pitch-standards generate one another: generating downward from above, all are three generating two; generating upward from below, all are three generating four.

sentences.zh: 陽下生陰，陰上生陽，終於中呂，而十二律畢矣。

translations.literal: Yang generates yin downward, yin generates yang upward, ending at Middle Pitch, and the twelve pitch-standards are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yang generates yin downward, yin generates yang upward, ending at Middle Pitch, and the twelve pitch-standards are complete.

sentences.zh: 中呂上生執始，執始下生去滅，上下相生，終於南事，六十律畢矣。

translations.literal: Middle Pitch generates upward to Holding Beginning; Holding Beginning generates downward to Departing Extinction; generating upward and downward, ending at Southern Affair, and the sixty pitch-standards are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Middle Pitch generates upward to Holding Beginning; Holding Beginning generates downward to Departing Extinction; generating upward and downward, ending at Southern Affair, and the sixty pitch-standards are complete.

sentences.zh: 十二律之變至於六十，猶八卦之變至於六十四也，冬至之聲，以黃鐘為宮，太簇為商，姑洗為角，林鐘為徵，南呂為羽，應鐘為變宮，蕤賓為變徵。

translations.literal: The transformation of the twelve pitch-standards into sixty is like the transformation of the eight trigrams into sixty-four; the sounds of the winter solstice take the Yellow Bell as tonic, Great Cluster as second, Maiden Wash as third, Forest Bell as fourth, Southern Pitch as fifth, Responding Bell as altered tonic, and Luxuriant Guest as altered fourth.
translations.idiomatic: The transformation of the twelve pitch-standards into sixty is like the transformation of the eight trigrams into sixty-four. The sounds of the winter solstice take the Yellow Bell as tonic, Great Cluster as second, Maiden Wash as third, Forest Bell as fourth, Southern Pitch as fifth, Responding Bell as altered tonic, and Luxuriant Guest as altered fourth.

sentences.zh: 此聲氣之元，五音之正也。

translations.literal: This is the origin of sound and qi, the correctness of the five tones.
translations.idiomatic: This is the origin of sound and qi, the correctness of the five tones.

sentences.zh: 故各統一日。

translations.literal: Therefore each governs one day.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore each governs one day.

sentences.zh: 其餘以次運行，當日者各自為宮，而商徵以類從焉。」

translations.literal: The rest operate in sequence; on its day each serves as tonic, and the second and fourth follow by kind.
translations.idiomatic: The rest operate in sequence. On its day each serves as tonic, and the second and fourth follow by kind.

sentences.zh: 房又曰：「竹聲不可以度調，故作準以定數。

translations.literal: Fang further said: "Bamboo sounds cannot be measured for tuning; therefore a pitch-pipe standard was made to fix the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Fang further said, "Bamboo sounds cannot be measured for tuning; therefore a pitch-pipe standard was made to fix the numbers.

sentences.zh: 准之狀如瑟，長一丈而十三弦，隱間九尺，以應黃鐘之律九寸。

translations.literal: The standard's form is like a se zither, one zhang long with thirteen strings; the hidden space nine chi, corresponding to the nine cun of the Yellow Bell pitch-standard.
translations.idiomatic: The standard's form is like a se zither, one zhang long with thirteen strings. The hidden space is nine chi, corresponding to the nine cun of the Yellow Bell pitch-standard.

sentences.zh: 中央一弦，下畫分寸，以為六十律清濁之節。」

translations.literal: On the central string, cun and fen are marked below, to serve as the nodes of clear and muddy for the sixty pitch-standards."
translations.idiomatic: On the central string, cun and fen are marked below to serve as the nodes of clear and muddy for the sixty pitch-standards."

sentences.zh: 執始之類，皆房自造。

translations.literal: Names like Holding Beginning were all invented by Fang himself.
translations.idiomatic: Names like Holding Beginning were all invented by Fang himself.

sentences.zh: 房雲受法于焦延壽，未知延壽所承也。

translations.literal: Fang said he received the method from Jiao Yanshou; it is not known from whom Yanshou received it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang said he received the method from Jiao Yanshou, but it is not known from whom Yanshou received it.

sentences.zh: 至元和年，待詔候鐘律殷肜上言：「官無曉六十律以准調音者。

translations.literal: By the Yuanhe era, Awaiting-Edict Yin Rong, who observed bells and pitch-standards, memorialized: "There is no official who understands the sixty pitch-standards and uses the standard to tune sounds.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yuanhe era, Awaiting-Edict Yin Rong, who observed bells and pitch-standards, memorialized, "There is no official who understands the sixty pitch-standards and uses the standard to tune sounds.

sentences.zh: 故待詔嚴崇具以准法教其子宣，願召宣補學官，主調樂器。」

translations.literal: Therefore Awaiting-Edict Yan Chong fully taught his son Xuan the method of the standard; he asked that Xuan be summoned to fill a learning office and take charge of tuning instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Awaiting-Edict Yan Chong fully taught his son Xuan the method of the standard and asked that Xuan be summoned to fill a learning office and take charge of tuning instruments.

sentences.zh: 大史丞弘試宣十二律，其二中，其四不中，其六不知何律，宣遂罷。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Assistant Hong tested Xuan on the twelve pitch-standards: two were correct, four were incorrect, and six he did not know which pitch-standard they were—Xuan was then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Assistant Hong tested Xuan on the twelve pitch-standards: two were correct, four were incorrect, and six he could not identify—Xuan was then dismissed.

sentences.zh: 自此律家莫能為准施弦。

translations.literal: From this time no pitch-standard specialist could apply the standard to string instruments.
translations.idiomatic: From this time no pitch-standard specialist could apply the standard to string instruments.

sentences.zh: 熹平年，東觀召典律者太子舍人張光問准意。

translations.literal: In the Xiping era, the Eastern View summoned Zhang Guang, Custodian of Pitch-Standards and Palace Attendant, to ask about the meaning of the standard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiping era, the Eastern View summoned Zhang Guang, Custodian of Pitch-Standards and Palace Attendant, to ask about the meaning of the standard.

sentences.zh: 光等不知，歸閱舊藏，乃得其器，形制如房書，猶不能定其弦緩急，故史官能辨清濁者遂絕。

translations.literal: Guang and the others did not know; returning to examine the old storehouse, they obtained the instrument, its form like Fang's book, yet still could not determine the tightness or looseness of its strings; thus the historiographers who could distinguish clear and muddy came to an end.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and the others did not know. Returning to examine the old storehouse, they obtained the instrument, its form matching Fang's description, yet still could not determine the tightness or looseness of its strings. Thus the historiographers who could distinguish clear and muddy tones died out.

sentences.zh: 其可以相傳者，唯大榷常數及候氣而已。

translations.literal: What could be handed down was only the great pitch-pipe constants and observing qi.
translations.idiomatic: What could be handed down was only the great pitch-pipe constants and the method of observing qi.

sentences.zh: 據此而論，京房之法，漢世已不能行。

translations.literal: Judged by this, Jing Fang's method could already not be implemented in Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by this, Jing Fang's method could already not be implemented in Han times.

sentences.zh: 沈約《宋志》曰：「詳案古典及今音家，六十律無施于樂。」

translations.literal: Shen Yue's Song Treatise says: "Examining the ancient classics and today's music specialists in detail, the sixty pitch-standards have no application in music.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue's Song Treatise says, "Examining the ancient classics and today's music specialists in detail, the sixty pitch-standards have no application in music.

sentences.zh: 《禮》雲「十二管還相為宮」，不言六十。

translations.literal: The Rites say "the twelve tubes cyclically generate the tonic"—they do not speak of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say "the twelve tubes cyclically generate the tonic"—they do not speak of sixty.

sentences.zh: 《封禪書》雲：「大帝使素女鼓五十弦瑟而悲，破為二十五弦。」

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices says: "The Great Emperor had the White Girl play the fifty-string se zither until it grew mournful, and it was broken into twenty-five strings.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices says, "The Great Emperor had the White Girl play the fifty-string se zither until it grew mournful, and it was broken into twenty-five strings.

sentences.zh: 假令六十律為樂，得成亦所不用。

translations.literal: Even if the sixty pitch-standards were made into music, even if they could be completed they would not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the sixty pitch-standards were made into music, even if they could be completed they would not be used.

sentences.zh: 取「大樂必易，大禮必簡」之意也。

translations.literal: This takes the meaning of "great music must be simple, great rites must be plain."
translations.idiomatic: This takes the meaning of "great music must be simple, great rites must be plain."

sentences.zh: 又議曰：

translations.literal: He further memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: He further memorialized:

sentences.zh: 案《周官》雲：「大司樂掌成均之法。」

translations.literal: According to the Offices of Zhou: "The Grand Master of Music is in charge of the method of completing the key.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Offices of Zhou, "The Grand Master of Music is in charge of the method of completing the key.

sentences.zh: 鄭眾注雲：「均，調也。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhong's commentary says: "Jun means tuning.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhong's commentary says, "Jun means tuning.

sentences.zh: 樂師主調其音。」

translations.literal: The music masters chiefly tune the sounds."
translations.idiomatic: The music masters chiefly tune the sounds."

sentences.zh: 《三禮義宗》稱：「《周官》奏黃鐘者，用黃鐘為調，歌大呂者，用大呂為調。

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Meaning of the Three Rites says: "When the Offices of Zhou play the Yellow Bell, they use the Yellow Bell as the key; when they sing the Great Mould, they use the Great Mould as the key.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Meaning of the Three Rites says, "When the Offices of Zhou play the Yellow Bell, they use the Yellow Bell as the key; when they sing the Great Mould, they use the Great Mould as the key.

sentences.zh: 奏者謂堂下四懸，歌者謂堂上所歌。

translations.literal: Playing refers to the four suspended sets below the hall; singing refers to what is sung above the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Playing refers to the four suspended sets below the hall; singing refers to what is sung above the hall.

sentences.zh: 但一祭之間，皆用二調。」

translations.literal: Yet within one sacrifice, two keys are used."
translations.idiomatic: Yet within one sacrifice, two keys are used."

sentences.zh: 是知據宮稱調，其義一也。

translations.literal: From this we know that taking the tonic as the key—the meaning is one.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that taking the tonic as the key—the meaning is the same.

sentences.zh: 明六律六呂迭相為宮，各自為調。

translations.literal: This shows that the six pitch-standards and six pitch-standards alternate as tonic, each serving as its own key.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the six pitch-standards and six pitch-standards alternate as tonic, each serving as its own key.

sentences.zh: 今見行之樂，用黃鐘之宮，乃以林鐘為調，與古典有違。

translations.literal: The music now in practice uses the Yellow Bell tonic, yet takes the Forest Bell as the key—this conflicts with the ancient classics.
translations.idiomatic: The music now in practice uses the Yellow Bell tonic, yet takes the Forest Bell as the key—this conflicts with the ancient classics.

sentences.zh: 晉內書監荀勖依典記，以五聲十二律還相為宮之法，制十二笛。

translations.literal: Jin Inner Secretariat Director Xun Xu, following the canonical records, made twelve flutes by the method of the five tones and twelve pitch-standards cyclically generating the tonic.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Inner Secretariat Director Xun Xu, following the canonical records, made twelve flutes by the method of the five tones and twelve pitch-standards cyclically generating the tonic.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘之笛，正聲應黃鐘，下徵應林鐘，以姑洗為清角。

translations.literal: The Yellow Bell flute: the principal sound responds to the Yellow Bell, the lower fourth responds to the Forest Bell, and Maiden Wash serves as the clear third.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell flute: the principal sound responds to the Yellow Bell, the lower fourth responds to the Forest Bell, and Maiden Wash serves as the clear third.

sentences.zh: 大呂之笛，正聲應大呂，下徵應夷則。

translations.literal: The Great Mould flute: the principal sound responds to the Great Mould, the lower fourth responds to Barren Rule.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Mould flute: the principal sound responds to the Great Mould, and the lower fourth responds to Barren Rule.

sentences.zh: 以外諸均，例皆如是。

translations.literal: The other keys all follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The other keys all follow this pattern.

sentences.zh: 然今所用林鐘，是勖下徵之調。

translations.literal: Yet the Forest Bell now in use is Xun Xu's lower-fourth key.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Forest Bell now in use is Xun Xu's lower-fourth key.

sentences.zh: 不取其正，先用其下，於理未通，故須改之。

translations.literal: Not taking the principal but first using the lower—this is not coherent in principle; therefore it must be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Not taking the principal but first using the lower—this is not coherent in principle. Therefore it must be changed.

sentences.zh: 上甚善其義，詔弘與姚察、許善心、何妥、虞世基等正定新樂，事在《音律志》。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly approved his reasoning and ordered Hong, together with Yao Cha, Xu Shanxin, He Tuo, Yu Shiji, and others to fix the new music—the matter is recorded in the Treatise on Pitch-Standards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly approved his reasoning and ordered Hong, together with Yao Cha, Xu Shanxin, He Tuo, Yu Shiji, and others to fix the new music. The matter is recorded in the Treatise on Pitch-Standards.

sentences.zh: 是後議置明堂，詔弘條上故事，議其得失，事在《禮志》。

translations.literal: After this, when the Bright Hall was deliberated, an edict ordered Hong to set forth precedents and discuss their merits and faults—the matter is recorded in the Treatise on Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After this, when the Bright Hall was deliberated, an edict ordered Hong to set forth precedents and discuss their merits and faults. The matter is recorded in the Treatise on Rites.

sentences.zh: 上甚敬重之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly respected and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly respected and honored him.

sentences.zh: 時楊素恃才矜貴，輕侮朝臣，唯見弘未當不改容自肅。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Su relied on his talent and prized his eminence, treating court ministers lightly; only when he saw Hong did he never fail to compose himself with reverence.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yang Su relied on his talent and prized his eminence, treating court ministers lightly. Only when he saw Hong did he never fail to compose himself with reverence.

sentences.zh: 素將擊突厥，詣太常與弘言別。

translations.literal: When Su was about to attack the Turks, he went to the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness to take leave of Hong.
translations.idiomatic: When Su was about to attack the Turks, he went to the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness to take leave of Hong.

sentences.zh: 弘送素至中門而止，素謂弘曰：「大將出征，故來敘別，何相送之近也？」

translations.literal: Hong escorted Su only to the middle gate and stopped. Su said to Hong: "A great general is going on campaign and came to take leave—why is your escort so short?
translations.idiomatic: Hong escorted Su only to the middle gate and stopped. Su said to Hong, "A great general is going on campaign and came to take leave—why is your escort so short?

sentences.zh: 弘遂揖而退。

translations.literal: Hong bowed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hong bowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 素笑曰：「奇章公可謂其智可及，其愚不可及也。」

translations.literal: Su laughed and said: "Duke of Qizhang may be said to have wisdom that can be matched, but foolishness that cannot be matched.
translations.idiomatic: Su laughed and said, "Duke of Qizhang may be said to have wisdom that can be matched, but foolishness that cannot be matched.

sentences.zh: 亦不以屑懷。

translations.literal: Hong also did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Hong also did not take it to heart.

sentences.zh: 尋授大將軍，拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand General and appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Grand General and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時高祖又令弘與楊素、蘇威、薛道衡、許善心、虞世基、崔子發等並召諸儒，論新禮降殺輕重。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gaozu also ordered Hong, together with Yang Su, Su Wei, Xue Daoheng, Xu Shanxin, Yu Shiji, Cui Zifa, and others, to summon the Confucians and discuss the gradations of increase and decrease in the new rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Gaozu also ordered Hong, together with Yang Su, Su Wei, Xue Daoheng, Xu Shanxin, Yu Shiji, Cui Zifa, and others, to summon the Confucians and discuss the gradations of increase and decrease in the new rites.

sentences.zh: 弘所立議，眾咸推服之。

translations.literal: The positions Hong established were all admired and accepted by the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: The positions Hong established were all admired and accepted by the assembly.

sentences.zh: 仁壽二年，獻皇后崩，三公已下不能定其儀注。

translations.literal: In the second year of Renshou, Empress Xian died, and from the Three Excellencies downward no one could fix the ritual procedures.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Renshou, Empress Xian died, and from the Three Excellencies downward no one could determine the ritual procedures.

sentences.zh: 楊素謂弘曰：「公舊學，時賢所仰，今日之事，決在於公。」

translations.literal: Yang Su said to Hong: "Your Lordship's long learning is admired by the worthies of the age; today's affair is decided by you.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su said to Hong, "Your Lordship's long learning is admired by the worthies of the age. Today's affair is decided by you.

sentences.zh: 弘了不辭讓，斯須之間，儀注悉備，皆有故實。

translations.literal: Hong did not decline at all; in a moment the ritual procedures were all complete, each with its precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Hong did not decline at all. In a moment the ritual procedures were all complete, each with its precedent.

sentences.zh: 素歎曰：「衣冠禮樂，盡在此矣，非吾所及也！」

translations.literal: Su sighed and said: "Robes and caps, rites and music—all are here; this is beyond what I can reach!
translations.idiomatic: Su sighed and said, "Robes and caps, rites and music—all are here. This is beyond what I can reach!

sentences.zh: 弘以三年之喪，祥禫具有降殺，期服十一月而練者，無所象法，以聞于高祖，高祖納焉。

translations.literal: Hong held that in the three-year mourning, the xiang and chan sacrifices have their gradations, but the practice of wearing mourning for eleven months with a practice garment has no symbolic model; he reported this to Emperor Gaozu, and Gaozu accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Hong held that in the three-year mourning, the xiang and chan sacrifices have their gradations, but the practice of wearing mourning for eleven months with a practice garment has no symbolic model. He reported this to Emperor Gaozu, and Gaozu accepted it.

sentences.zh: 下詔除期練之禮，自弘始也。

translations.literal: An edict was issued abolishing the practice-garment rite of the eleven-month mourning period—this began with Hong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued abolishing the practice-garment rite of the eleven-month mourning period. This reform began with Hong.

sentences.zh: 弘在吏部，其選舉先德行而後文才，務在審慎。

translations.literal: When Hong was in the Ministry of Personnel, in selections he put virtue and conduct first and literary talent second, striving for careful judgment.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong was in the Ministry of Personnel, in selections he put virtue and conduct first and literary talent second, striving for careful judgment.

sentences.zh: 雖致停緩，所有進用，並多稱職。

translations.literal: Although this caused delays, of those promoted and employed, most proved competent in their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Although this caused delays, most of those promoted and employed proved competent in their posts.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎高孝基，鑒賞機晤，清慎絕倫，然爽俊有餘，跡似輕薄，時宰多以此疑之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Gao Xiaoji had discerning judgment and quick wit, and his purity and caution were unmatched; yet he had excess of bold brilliance and his conduct seemed somewhat frivolous, and the chief ministers often doubted him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Gao Xiaoji had discerning judgment and quick wit, and his purity and caution were unmatched. Yet he had an excess of bold brilliance and his conduct seemed somewhat frivolous, and the chief ministers often doubted him for this.

sentences.zh: 唯弘深識其真，推心委任。

translations.literal: Only Hong deeply recognized his true worth and entrusted him with full confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hong deeply recognized his true worth and entrusted him with full confidence.

sentences.zh: 隋之選舉，於斯為最。

translations.literal: Sui's selections reached their highest point at this time.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui dynasty's personnel selections reached their highest point at this time.

sentences.zh: 時論彌服弘識度之遠。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion increasingly admired Hong's far-reaching discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion increasingly admired Hong's far-reaching discernment.

sentences.zh: 煬帝之在東宮也，數有詩書遺弘，弘亦有答。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was in the Eastern Palace, he often sent poems and letters to Hong, and Hong also replied.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang was crown prince, he often sent poems and letters to Hong, and Hong also replied.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位之後，嘗賜弘詩曰：「晉家山吏部，魏世盧尚書，莫言先哲異，奇才並佐餘。

translations.literal: After he succeeded to the throne, he once bestowed a poem on Hong, saying: "The Jin dynasty had the Minister of the Mountain; the Wei age had Minister Lu—do not say the former sages differ; rare talents alike assist me.
translations.idiomatic: After he succeeded to the throne, he once bestowed a poem on Hong, saying, "The Jin dynasty had the Minister of the Mountain; the Wei age had Minister Lu—do not say the former sages differ; rare talents alike assist me.

sentences.zh: 學行敦時俗，道素乃沖虛，納言雲閣上，禮儀皇運初。

translations.literal: Learning and conduct solidify the customs of the age; the Way's plainness is serene and empty; as Attendant-in-Ordinary above the Cloud Pavilion, rites and propriety mark the beginning of the imperial fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Learning and conduct solidify the customs of the age; the Way's plainness is serene and unassuming; as Attendant-in-Ordinary above the Cloud Pavilion, rites and propriety mark the beginning of the imperial fortune.

sentences.zh: 彝倫欣有敘，垂拱事端居。」

translations.literal: The constant norms rejoice in good order; with hands draped in the sleeves, affairs are calmly settled.
translations.idiomatic: The constant norms rejoice in good order; with hands draped in the sleeves, affairs are calmly settled.

sentences.zh: 其同被賜詩者，至於文詞讚揚，無如弘美。

translations.literal: Of those who likewise received bestowed poems, in literary praise none was as beautiful as Hong's.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who likewise received bestowed poems, in literary praise none was as beautiful as Hong's.

sentences.zh: 大業二年，進位上大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daye, he was advanced to Grand General of the Upper Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daye, he was advanced to Grand General of the Upper Rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，改為右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was changed to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, he was appointed Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 從拜恆嶽，壇場珪幣，墠畤牲牢，並弘所定。

translations.literal: Accompanying the worship at Mount Heng, the altar grounds, jade and silks, the open-air altar and sacrificial animals—all were fixed by Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the worship at Mount Heng, the altar grounds, jade and silks, the open-air altar and sacrificial animals—all were fixed by Hong.

sentences.zh: 還下太行，煬帝嘗引入內帳，對皇后賜以同席飲食。

translations.literal: Returning down from the Taihang Mountains, Emperor Yang once brought him into the inner tent and, facing the empress, granted him food and drink at the same mat.
translations.idiomatic: Returning down from the Taihang Mountains, Emperor Yang once brought him into the inner tent and, in the empress's presence, granted him food and drink at the same mat.

sentences.zh: 其禮遇親重如此。

translations.literal: His courtesy and intimate honor were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: His courtesy and intimate honor were such as this.

sentences.zh: 弘謂其諸子曰：「吾受非常之遇，荷恩深重。

translations.literal: Hong said to his sons: "I have received an extraordinary favor and bear a deep debt of grace.
translations.idiomatic: Hong said to his sons, "I have received an extraordinary favor and bear a deep debt of grace.

sentences.zh: 汝等子孫，宜以誠敬自立，以答恩遇之隆也。」

translations.literal: You, my sons and descendants, should establish yourselves with sincerity and reverence, to repay this lofty favor.
translations.idiomatic: You, my sons and descendants, should establish yourselves with sincerity and reverence to repay this lofty favor.

sentences.zh: 六年，從幸江都。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，卒于江都郡，時年六十六。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, he died in Jiangdu Commandery at the age of sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year, he died in Jiangdu Commandery at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 帝傷惜之，贈甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved for him and granted posthumous honors very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved for him and granted posthumous honors very generously.

sentences.zh: 歸葬安定，贈開府儀同三司、光祿大夫、文安侯，諡曰憲。

translations.literal: He was buried in Anding; posthumously granted the privileges of the Three Excellencies with an office, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Marquis of Wen'an; his posthumous name was Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in Anding. He was posthumously granted the privileges of the Three Excellencies with an office, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Marquis of Wen'an. His posthumous name was Xian.

sentences.zh: 弘榮寵當世，而車服卑儉，事上盡禮，待下以仁，訥於言而敏於行。

translations.literal: Hong enjoyed glory and favor in his age, yet his carriage and robes were humble and plain; in serving his superiors he fulfilled all rites, in treating subordinates he used benevolence; he was slow of speech but quick in action.
translations.idiomatic: Hong enjoyed glory and favor in his age, yet his carriage and robes were humble and plain. In serving his superiors he fulfilled all rites; in treating subordinates he used benevolence. He was slow of speech but quick in action.

sentences.zh: 上嘗令其宣敕，弘至階下，不能言，退還拜謝，雲：「並忘之。」

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered him to proclaim an edict; Hong reached the foot of the steps but could not speak; returning he bowed in apology and said: "I have forgotten it all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ordered him to proclaim an edict. Hong reached the foot of the steps but could not speak. Returning, he bowed in apology and said, "I have forgotten it all.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「傳語小辯，故非宰臣任也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Transmitting words is a minor skill; therefore it is not the task of a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Transmitting words is a minor skill; therefore it is not the task of a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 愈稱其質直。

translations.literal: He praised his plainness and directness all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He praised his plainness and directness all the more.

sentences.zh: 大業之世，委遇彌隆。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, his entrustment and favor grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era, his entrustment and favor grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 性寬厚，篤志於學，雖職務繁雜，書不釋手。

translations.literal: His nature was generous and broad; he was devoted to learning; although his duties were numerous and complex, he never put down his books.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was generous and broad, and he was devoted to learning. Although his duties were numerous and complex, he never put down his books.

sentences.zh: 隋室舊臣，始終信任，悔吝不及，唯弘一人而已。

translations.literal: Of the old ministers of the Sui house, from beginning to end trusted without regret or remorse—only Hong alone.
translations.idiomatic: Of the old ministers of the Sui house, only Hong alone was trusted from beginning to end without regret or remorse.

sentences.zh: 有弟曰弼，好酒而酗，嘗因醉，射殺弘駕車牛。

translations.literal: He had a younger brother named Bi who loved wine and drank to excess; once while drunk he shot and killed the ox that drew Hong's carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He had a younger brother named Bi who loved wine and drank to excess. Once while drunk he shot and killed the ox that drew Hong's carriage.

sentences.zh: 弘來還宅，其妻迎謂之曰：「叔射殺牛矣。」

translations.literal: When Hong returned home, his wife met him and said: "Your younger brother has shot and killed the ox.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong returned home, his wife met him and said, "Your younger brother has shot and killed the ox.

sentences.zh: 弘聞之，無所怪問，直答雲：「作脯。」

translations.literal: Hearing this, Hong asked nothing in surprise and simply replied: "Make jerky."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Hong asked nothing in surprise and simply replied, "Make jerky."

sentences.zh: 坐定，其妻又曰：「叔忽射殺牛，大是異事！」

translations.literal: When he was seated, his wife again said: "Your younger brother suddenly shot and killed the ox—a most unusual affair!"
translations.idiomatic: When he was seated, his wife again said, "Your younger brother suddenly shot and killed the ox—a most unusual affair!"

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「已知之矣。」

translations.literal: Hong said: "I already know."
translations.idiomatic: Hong said, "I already know."

sentences.zh: 顏色自若，讀書不輟。

translations.literal: His expression was as calm as before, and he did not stop reading.
translations.idiomatic: His expression remained calm, and he did not stop reading.

sentences.zh: 其寬和如此。

translations.literal: His generosity and mildness were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: His generosity and mildness were such as this.

sentences.zh: 有文集十三卷行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings in thirteen scrolls circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He had collected writings in thirteen scrolls circulating in the world.

sentences.zh: 長子方大，亦有學業，官至內史舍人。

translations.literal: His eldest son Fangda also had learning and reached the office of Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Fangda also had learning and reached the office of Secretariat Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 次子方裕，性兇險無人心，從幸江都，與裴虔通等同謀弑逆，事見《司馬德勘傳》。

translations.literal: His second son Fangyu had a fierce and treacherous nature devoid of human feeling; accompanying the emperor to Jiangdu, he joined Pei Qiantong and others in plotting regicide—the matter is recorded in the biography of Sima Dekan.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Fangyu had a fierce and treacherous nature devoid of human feeling. Accompanying the emperor to Jiangdu, he joined Pei Qiantong and others in plotting regicide. The matter is recorded in the biography of Sima Dekan.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：牛弘篤好墳籍，學優而仕，有淡雅之風，懷曠遠之度，采百王之損益，成一代之典章，漢之叔孫，不能尚也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Niu Hong deeply loved the classics and records, entered office through superior learning, had a refined and plain style, and bore a broad and far-reaching measure; gathering the additions and subtractions of a hundred kings, he completed the statutes of an age—even Shusun of Han cannot be placed above him.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Niu Hong deeply loved the classics and records, entered office through superior learning, had a refined and plain style, and bore a broad and far-reaching measure. Gathering the additions and subtractions of a hundred kings, he completed the statutes of an age—even Shusun of Han cannot be placed above him.

sentences.zh: 綢繆省闥，三十餘年，夷險不渝，始終無際。

translations.literal: Attending closely in the inner court for more than thirty years, through peace and peril he did not change; from beginning to end there was no break.
translations.idiomatic: Attending closely in the inner court for more than thirty years, through peace and peril he did not change. From beginning to end there was no break.

sentences.zh: 雖開物成務，非其所長，然澄之不清，混之不濁，可謂大雅君子矣。

translations.literal: Although opening things and completing affairs were not his special strengths, yet clarified he was not made clear, mixed he was not made muddy—he may be called a great refined gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Although opening things and completing affairs were not his special strengths, yet clarified he was not made clear, mixed he was not made muddy—he may be called a great refined gentleman.

sentences.zh: 子實不才，崇基不構，干紀犯義，以墜家風，惜哉！

translations.literal: His son was truly without talent, the lofty foundation was not built up, he violated the statutes and transgressed righteousness, and thereby ruined the family tradition—alas!
translations.idiomatic: His son was truly without talent, the lofty foundation was not built up, he violated the statutes and transgressed righteousness, and thereby ruined the family tradition—alas!
